entry.title: Visual attribution limits and graded provenance auditing for commercial video-generation APIs
entry.summary: Visual Attribution Limits and Graded Provenance Auditing in Commercial Video-Generation APIs arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper examines whether a delivered video file can establish which model or tier produced it, when intermediaries might substitute cheaper models or cached clips. It combines passive attribution probes with cryptographic provenance checks such as C2PA across 19 commercial endpoints. The authors conclude that only authenticated provenance supports accusations, while passive detection accuracy drops sharply after re-encoding.

entry.title: Classical oracle separation of QMA from the QCMA hierarchy and quantum cryptography, even when P = QCMA
entry.summary: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces a new problem called Codeword-Hash pairs in Noise (CHN) and proves, in the query complexity model, that it lies in QMA but is hard for the QCMA hierarchy (QCMAH). Using this problem, it constructs a classical oracle under which QMA is strictly more powerful than QCMAH. The paper also shows that, relative to an oracle where P = QCMA, various quantum cryptographic primitives, such as pseudorandom states with classical keys, can still exist. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce CHN, prove a classical-oracle separation of QMA from the QCMA hierarchy, and answer an open question of Kretschmer, Qian, and Tal.

entry.title: GEOHunter: Tracing a Paid Promotion Network That Influences AI Search Answers
entry.summary: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines a network that sells visibility in AI-generated answers by publishing paid promotional articles on three major Chinese user-generated-content platforms. The authors identified 1,985 associated accounts and 466,357 inferred promotional placements spanning multiple months and product categories. Across nine generative engines from the US and China, 4.5% to 20% of retrievable cited pages were attributable to the network, and its clients were named in 52% of answers on eight engines. The authors conclude that content-level defenses are insufficient, and that account-level and platform-level signals are needed. ★★★★ Notable: The authors measure a paid GEO content network across three platforms, identifying 1,985 accounts and 466,357 placements and assessing impact on nine generative engines.

entry.title: Replicating AI Agent Security Incidents for Audit (ROGUE-AI)
entry.summary: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI) arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents ROGUE-AI, a multi-agent framework that rebuilds reported incidents involving LLM-based agents offline, paired with a control lacking only the blamed cause. Across 108 attempted replications, about 89% reproduced the reported harm. Most replications had no attacker, and agents missed ordinary hazards while doing their assigned tasks, causing more harm than prompt-injection replications. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors rebuild 108 real incidents with matched controls lacking the blamed cause, reporting 89% harm reproduction and 18% to 33% error rates across five models.

entry.title: Front-running attack via causal overtaking in fair transaction ordering
entry.summary: Causal Overtaking in Fair Transaction Ordering arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies an attack on fair transaction ordering protocols, in which corrupted replicas observe a target transaction and submit identical signed copies of a responsive transaction through multiple client entries, so the response executes before its target. The authors formalize a class of receipt-order protocols, including Themis, and characterize the timing and network conditions under which the attack is feasible. They prove that receipt-only mechanisms cannot always preserve earlier-submission priority while preventing responsive overtaking. A mitigation is proposed and analyzed, and both the attack and the mitigation are evaluated through simulations using AWS and WonderProxy latency measurements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify causal overtaking across multiple client entries and prove receipt-only evidence cannot always preserve priority; simulations use AWS and WonderProxy latencies on Themis.

entry.title: BlockJack: Cross-tenant redirection fault attacks on paged KV cache in LLM serving
entry.summary: BlockJack: Cross-Tenant Redirection Fault Attacks on Paged KV Cache Address Translation in LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents BlockJack, the first fault attack targeting KV cache address translation in LLM inference. By corrupting block-table entries in vLLM, it redirects one request's KV cache reads to blocks belonging to another tenant, without changing model weights, prompts, or cached states. The authors show across seven models that victim context can be exposed and responses can be steered, and demonstrate physical feasibility with Rowhammer. They also evaluate assignment validation as a defense. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first fault attack on paged KV cache address translation in LLM serving, where block-table corruption redirects reads across tenants. entry.title: A review of how LLM capability in software vulnerability research has evolved
entry.summary: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a framework that rates LLM-based agents' ability to discover, validate and patch vulnerabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on driving automation levels, and systematizes the published evidence. It analyzes a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data, finding that disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled in 2026 with a rising share rated critical or high. The time between report and fix, and between disclosure and attack, has not noticeably changed so far. The authors also grade proposed mitigations with an explicit rubric.

entry.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
entry.summary: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces EditSafetyBench, a benchmark of 5,940 image-instruction pairs covering 11 risk categories and three edit intents, for measuring the safety awareness of image editing systems. Four systems, Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local, were evaluated on it. The authors find that these systems refuse far more often when the text prompt is unsafe than when the uploaded image is unsafe with a neutral instruction. They conclude that safety guardrails should reason jointly over both visual and textual inputs.

entry.title: Tracing security incidents in AI agent apps with Origin, a tool that finds entry points
entry.summary: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses how organizations investigate security incidents in agent applications by tracing back to the compromise entry point (CEP). Because trajectory logs describe agent functionality while CEP candidates are code-level function calls, analysts must manually map between the two. The authors present Origin, which uses a cross-layer dependency graph, a query language, and a region inference algorithm to link these semantic layers. In case studies on five popular agent applications across eight attack incidents, an analyst using Origin correctly identified all CEPs.

entry.title: Optimizing honeypot-based detection of insider threats through accumulating evidence
entry.summary: When Suspicion Adds Up: A Stochastic Framework for Optimizing Honeypot-Based Insider-Threat Detection arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a decision framework for detecting insider threats, where trusted users misuse their access to organizational systems. It models evidence accumulated from honeypot interactions as a continuous-time Markov chain and jointly selects the number of honeypots and the monitoring horizon to minimize expected losses from malicious activity and false detections. For thresholds of two and three interactions, the authors derive closed-form true- and false-detection probabilities and expected detection times, and present numerical results.

entry.title: DailySafe: A benchmark for testing whether AI models stay safe during everyday multi-turn, multi-image conversations
entry.summary: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces DailySafe, a benchmark for evaluating how well multimodal large language models maintain dynamic safety awareness in everyday interactions. It contains 195 naturalistic multi-turn, multi-image conversations spanning 10 daily domains and 42 task categories. Safety-critical evidence is revealed gradually across dialogue turns and visual observations, and the benchmark checks whether models recognize evolving risks while still supporting users' legitimate goals.

entry.title: A paper on products of distinguisher hulls
entry.summary: Products of Distinguisher Hulls arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how the distinguisher hull of two distributions, the convex hull of acceptance-probability pairs for tests in a given class, behaves under independent products for size-bounded Boolean circuits. It derives a geometric consequence of Dwork and Tankala's supersimulator theorem (FOCS 2026) and gives a substantially different proof of approximate product containment for distinguisher hulls. The construction uses nonadaptive sampling instead of adaptive score corrections.

entry.title: SCARVA: A framework for trustworthy, explainable AI-agent analysis of software supply-chain vulnerabilities
entry.summary: SCARVA: Interpretable Agentic Reasoning in Software Supply-Chain Analysis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Applications can inherit security vulnerabilities from their dependencies, but a vulnerable dependency does not always put the application at risk. The paper presents SCARVA, which has an analyst agent assess software security while logging every tool call, file access, and web request, and independent judge agents then review the analysis to produce an evidence-backed report. Tested on 54 manually curated cases, the best analyst model, Qwen 3.8, reached 82% balanced accuracy. Human annotators agreed with the best judge model, Claude Opus 5.5, in 94% of claim checks.

entry.title: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ChronoPatch, a black-box attack that makes vision-language models generate longer responses using adversarial visual inputs, requiring only access to the final response. Experiments on four open-source models and three commercial APIs show increased inference latency, higher GPU energy consumption, and more repetitive outputs. The authors conclude that this generation-based availability risk persists even when attackers see only final responses, and they call for generation-aware safeguards for deployed generative AI services.

entry.title: Phantom of the Masquerade: GNN-based detection of impersonation attacks on car and industrial control networks
entry.summary: Phantom of the Masquerade: Graph Neural Network-Based Detection of Masquerade Attacks in Controller Area Networks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses masquerade attacks on controller area networks (CANs), which lack built-in security and can be used to inject messages that mimic legitimate traffic. The authors propose PhantoMasq, a graph neural network framework that models CAN traffic as message sequence graphs enriched with lightweight signal statistics and classifies them with graph convolutional networks. On the ROAD dataset, it achieves mean AUC-ROC between 0.831 and 0.999 across five attack types and outperforms a state-of-the-art graph-embedding baseline on all of them.

entry.title: Detecting GNSS spoofing that keeps drone swarm formation by using transmitter parallax
entry.summary: Detecting Formation-Preserving GNSS Spoofing of UAV Swarms through Transmitter Parallax in Pseudorange and Doppler arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Drone swarms usually detect GNSS spoofing by comparing reported positions with their known formation, but formation-preserving spoofing evades this check. The paper proposes a likelihood ratio test that uses the pseudoranges and Doppler each drone already measures to detect the parallax left by nearby transmitters, without extra antennas. Simulations show it detects GNSS-WASP attacks at higher rates than the proposed countermeasure, and also catches single-transmitter and ground-array spoofing.

entry.title: Ask First, Then Affirm: Restoring Commitment Does Not Restore Refusal
entry.summary: Question, Then Affirm: Restoring Commitment Does Not Restore Refusal arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper finds that image generation safeguards can be bypassed without changing a message's meaning. A sign stating a harmful claim is blocked, but the same claim phrased as a question with a check mark is generated, and the image still endorses the original claim. The authors call this Deferred Semantic Commitment (DSC) and compare gpt-image-2 on a 300-case challenge set.

entry.title: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Agent for Classifying Threats and Suggesting Responses
entry.summary: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents RAVEN, an agent framework that helps security operations center analysts by automating the initial stages of security alert investigation. It uses a Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach to provide an initial classification of security events, which analysts can refine through interactive queries. The system is said to generate remediation suggestions tailored to the target enterprise's infrastructure rather than generic strategies. The authors report preliminary results on three test sets of 400 web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative mitigation case study.

entry.title: ALIoTh: Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated IoT Penetration Testing
entry.summary: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ALIoTh, a framework in which multiple large language model agents, orchestrated via LangGraph and enhanced with a Self-RAG architecture, autonomously find and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and industrial IoT environments. It covers the full offensive pipeline, including network and device enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation. The Self-RAG mechanism gives expert agents access to IoT security knowledge such as documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques.

entry.title: Checking CyberGym: Are Vulnerability Reproduction Scores Reliable?
entry.summary: On the Reliability of CyberGym Evaluation: Task Material Consistency and Reference-Target Identity arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether CyberGym, a benchmark for vulnerability reproduction, yields reliable scores. The benchmark counts a proof-of-concept input as successful if it crashes the vulnerable program but not the fixed version. The authors audit all 1,507 tasks and find inconsistent task materials in 338 of them (22.4%). They also check the identity of final inputs from one run and find that many passing inputs trigger a non-target defect, lowering the pass rate from 85.3% to 78.8% when a target hit is required.

entry.title: A defense that makes JavaScript programs harder for AI agents to scan for vulnerabilities
entry.summary: Hardening JavaScript Programs against LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents AntiAgent, a method that transforms JavaScript programs before release so that LLM-based vulnerability detection agents have trouble finding their flaws. It evolves programs with known vulnerabilities and turns the transformations that evade detection into reusable rules. On real-world JavaScript applications against four detection agents, including Claude Code and Codex, it cut detected vulnerabilities by 52.0-60.7%, and the transformed programs passed all project tests.

entry.title: Asking in a crowd: privacy-protected AI queries by mixing in fake ones
entry.summary: Ask in the Crowd: Differentially Private LLM Inference via Dummy-Augmented Shuffling arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes DP-SPD, a framework that protects user queries sent to remote large language models. The real query is hidden among dummy queries generated on the client side, and all queries are randomly shuffled before reaching the server. The method also reuses transformer key-value caches across the shared prefixes of queries to improve inference efficiency.

entry.title: GPU-accelerated secure prediction of drug-target interactions
entry.summary: GPU-Accelerated Secure Inference for Drug--Target Interaction Prediction arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a method for predicting drug-target interactions with two servers, so that neither server learns the secret drug being scored. The authors design SlimDTA, a model that reduces the non-linear operations requiring communication, and build a GPU framework using additive and function secret sharing. The solution won first place in Track III of the iDASH 2026 competition, averaging under 10 ms per prediction. Its secure predictions match the plaintext model to within 0.02%.

entry.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage in Shared Embeddings
entry.summary: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how shared foundation-model embeddings, such as medical-image features, can reveal sensitive attributes. It proves that when task and sensitive labels are associated, global and task-conditional linear guardedness cannot both hold while preserving a linear task signal. The authors propose TC-LEACE, a closed-form variant of LEACE that enforces linear guardedness within each task stratum. Experiments on 85 CelebA attribute pairs and hospital chest radiographs show that conditional leakage persists after LEACE, and TC-LEACE recovers most of the task-utility loss while keeping conditional leakage near LEACE's level.

entry.title: MetaScanner: Study and Defense Against Deceptive UI Attacks in Social VR
entry.summary: MetaScanner: An Empirical Study and Proactive Defense against Deceptive UI Attacks in Social VR arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces four new deceptive user interface attacks that secretly trick users of social VR platforms into performing unintended actions. The attacks were implemented on VRChat, and a user study with 30 IRB-approved participants confirmed their effectiveness. The authors also propose MetaScanner, a system that scans virtual world scripts and interactive objects to find suspicious elements before users encounter them. It detected all threats in test worlds and averaged 5 seconds of scanning time across 38 real-world assets.

entry.title: Tether: A Verified Stateful Policy Engine for Monitoring AI Agents at the System Level
entry.summary: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents Tether, a framework that enforces stateful security policies at runtime over the side effects of AI agents' actions. Each proposed action runs in an isolated sandbox, and its semantics are inferred from observed system calls before it is allowed to proceed. Policies are written in an embedded domain-specific language in Lean 4, which allows formal verification of global security invariants. On coding-agent benchmarks, a single shared policy reportedly blocks 100% of in-scope attacks with a benign false-positive rate under 5%.

entry.title: Measuring Hallucination in LLMs for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
entry.summary: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines how often large language models make up false or unsupported content when summarizing or answering questions about cyber threat intelligence. The authors introduce HalluVision, a reproducible framework that extracts domain entities and scores factual consistency with several similarity metrics. They test two commercial models and one open-weight model on 4,940 real cybersecurity articles, validating results against 100 human-annotated outputs. Semantic similarity agrees with human judgments, while entity-based metrics show limited agreement.

entry.title: AZOWL AgentOps: Task-Scoped Governance for Deployed Agent Applications
entry.summary: AZOWL AgentOps: Task-Scoped Governance for Deployed Agent Applications arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents AZOWL AgentOps, a shared governance framework for deploying AI agents and delegating work to them. Accepted tasks receive a stable identifier linking the sender's authority, the assigned runner, required approvals, and result evidence. In 28 synthetic runs across four paired pilots, the authors compare AZOWL components with a configured LangGraph application. Both setups recorded zero business tasks in dialogue, rejected unauthorized agent handoffs, and issued zero writes when an approved delivery address changed.

entry.title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, Detection Benchmark and Audit of Image Ciphers
entry.summary: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of Published Image Ciphers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper examines NPCR, the share of ciphertext bytes changed by a one-pixel plaintext change, which is often cited as evidence of diffusion in image ciphers. It separates three regimes: no propagation, one round of linear chaining, and independent ciphertexts, and derives exact counts and spread signatures for telling them apart. The authors audit twenty-one published schemes against these signatures and release a checker for published tables. The checker shows what a table measures under stated assumptions but does not certify security.

entry.title: UniReFP: Robust Unified Fingerprinting for Vision Models Against Cross-Task Repurposing
entry.summary: UniReFP: Robust Unified Fingerprinting for Vision Models against Cross-Task Repurposing Attacks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper identifies a new attack, cross-task model repurposing, that can make existing model fingerprints unusable. It proposes UniReFP, a unified fingerprinting framework that verifies ownership in a shared class-level semantic space using a surrogate classifier and grouped fingerprints. Experiments reportedly show it performs better under cross-task repurposing, common model modification attacks, and their combinations.

entry.title: LingSante MedGuard: A Unified Guardrail Model for Detecting Risks in Medical AI Responses
entry.summary: LingSante MedGuard Technical Report arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This technical report introduces LingSante MedGuard, a guardrail model that combines supervision from a medical guardrail teacher and six specialized capability experts to detect safety, compliance, and ethical risks in medical AI responses. It is trained through supervised fine-tuning on teacher demonstrations followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors also present LingSante MedGuardBench, an 11-subset risk-detection benchmark. The model achieves mean F1 scores of 82.3%, 82.4%, and 87.4% at 4B, 9B, and 27B scales.

entry.title: Critical Review of Backtesting Validity in LLM Trading Agent Evaluations
entry.summary: Evaluating LIM Trading Agents: A Critical Review of Backtesting Validity and Reporting Practices arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines how large language models used in investment research are evaluated through backtesting. The authors identify six common threats to validity and apply them to 18 published studies, assessing 108 items in total. They find substantial reporting gaps, with only four studies providing minimal evidence across multiple market periods. The paper also proposes an evaluation protocol for future LLM investment research. Correction Nov 20, 2026: Marked withdrawn by its source; no longer a pick

entry.title: Power-analysis attack study on SHA-2-based SLH-DSA signatures
entry.summary: Correlation Power Analysis of SHA-2-Based SLH-DSA IACR ePrint · Nov 4, 2026This paper applies non-profiled correlation power analysis to the address-based pseudorandom function of SLH-DSA across all six SHA-2 parameter sets, targeting SHA-256 compression rounds and message-schedule expansion. Experiments on an STM32F303 ARM Cortex-M4 used 30 secret seeds with 5,000 power traces per seed. Reported rates are conditional stage-wise results with preceding secret values supplied correctly, not end-to-end seed recovery rates. The authors conclude that side-channel protection must cover both compression rounds and message-schedule expansion. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a staged non-profiled correlation power attack on SHA-2 SLH-DSA, covering compression rounds and message schedule, evaluated on an STM32F303 Cortex-M4.

entry.title: ToolPulse: Cache Side-Channel Eavesdropping on Tool-Using LLM Agents
entry.summary: ToolPulse: Side-Channel Eavesdropping on Tool-Using LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper shows that although commercial LLM inference runs remotely, the tools agents invoke execute on the user's machine and often rely on shared system libraries, creating a cache-based side-channel risk. The authors compare Flush+Reload and Prime+Probe and present ToolPulse, a framework whose Tool Recovery Attack reconstructs tool workflows across 11 LLMs on Codex and Claude Code with a lowest F1 score above 93%. Two further attacks, Task Profiling and Trigger Localization, infer user intent and identify sensitive tool calls, and they retain high accuracy even on a server shared by about 20 users. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors exploit cache side channels on shared libraries to eavesdrop on remote agents' tool calls, reporting F1 above 93% across 11 LLMs and robustness under noise.

entry.title: Using LLM Agents to Build Post-Quantum Crypto Hardware: What Tests and Reviews Miss
entry.summary: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a seven-stage verification-gated workflow in which LLM agents generate RTL for ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 accelerators, ported to a Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card. The authors audit the agent-generated evidence using netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. They find that existing simulation gates kill only 76% of mutants, and that module-scoped LLM review and formal checks detect flaws that broader review and tests miss. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit LLM-generated post-quantum RTL with netlist mutants and formal checks, reporting kill rates and review-session detection rates on an ML-KEM/ML-DSA accelerator.

entry.title: Recovering Verified RTL from Netlists Using LLM Agents
entry.summary: Verified Netlist-to-RTL Recovery with LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes LOCA (LOgic Cone Attack), which splits an anonymized gate-level netlist into logic cones that parallel LLM agents rewrite into compact RTL. Only RTL proven equivalent to the netlist is kept, and quality is measured by compression. Across 21 model-design pairs, LOCA recovers 17, compared with 6 using whole-netlist prompting. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors split netlists into logic cones rewritten by parallel LLM agents with equivalence proofs, recovering 17 of 21 model-design pairs versus 6 for whole-netlist prompting.

entry.title: Abusing browser-embedded local language models for post-exploitation attacks
entry.summary: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether language models built into browsers, such as Gemini Nano in Chrome, could be used by attackers after they gain access to a host. The authors report that the model can be driven using only interpreters that ship with the operating system, and that the user-activation check before download can be satisfied with a simulated click or bypassed. They also measure the model's ability to find credentials, detect PII in email, classify images, and call custom tools. Combining these abilities, they carry out a simulated operation with no user interaction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show browser-embedded local models can serve as post-exploitation engines, bypassing the activation check, and report capability tests plus an end-to-end simulated operation.

entry.title: Independent side-channel analysis of the RP2350 Challenge 2 AES implementation
entry.summary: Side-Channel Analysis of the RP2350 Challenge 2 arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an independent side-channel analysis of the hardened AES implementation in the RP2350 challenge. It covers leakage detection, plaintext dependence, and key extraction. The authors report weaknesses that contradict the challenge authors' claims and openly share the analysis to encourage further public scrutiny.

entry.title: VisualJevBench: A Benchmark and Black-Box Attacks for Image-Based Structured Decision Models
entry.summary: VisualJevBench: A Benchmark and Black-Box Attacks for Visual Typed Decision Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies the robustness of typed decision models that return structured decisions, extended to accept image inputs. It introduces VisualJevBench, a benchmark of 800 images and 3,200 questions across eight scenarios and four visual attack types. The authors also propose ABPS, a black-box method that uses typed-output feedback to find effective image manipulations, including universal attacks that transfer to unseen images and scenarios. Experiments on jev-1.14.0 report image-specific attack success rates up to 69.6%, universal attacks averaging 33.15% on unseen images, and geometric transformations averaging 40.09% in cross-scenario transfer.

entry.title: ChainAgent: Automated Discovery of Chainable Vulnerabilities in PHP Web Apps
entry.summary: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ChainAgent, an LLM-agent framework that jointly finds components of exploit chains and their capability dependencies in PHP web application source code. It is guided by an empirical study of 386 real-world web exploit chains. On 15 PHP applications, ChainAgent reaches 42.02%–44.63% recall for goal-reaching components and recovers up to 4.4 times as many correct goal-reaching dependency edges as the general-purpose coding agent Codex. On a further 30 real-world PHP applications, it identifies 20 vulnerabilities and 13 exploit chains, nine of which achieve remote code execution.

entry.title: SplitReAlign: A Partition-Aware Method for Unlearning in Split Federated Learning
entry.summary: SplitReAlign: Partition-Aware Representation Realignment for Split Federated Unlearning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes SplitReAlign, a framework for removing class-specific knowledge in split federated learning, where neural networks are divided between clients and a server. It builds endpoint-specific subspaces linked by a shared semantic anchor, realigning forgotten representations while penalizing changes outside active subspaces. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with heterogeneous client distributions report the lowest average gap to retraining across six settings.

entry.title: TRACE-5G: Trust-aware runtime attestation for continuous 5G device control
entry.summary: TRACE-5G: Trust-Aware Runtime Attestation and Continuous Enforcement for 5G User Equipment arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper notes that the standard 5G-AKA protocol verifies subscriber credentials but not the integrity of user equipment, and that existing certificate and TPM boot checks cannot detect unauthorized software run after admission. The authors propose TRACE-5G, which uses IMA, TPM, and Keylime to continuously verify the device's runtime software state and controls network access based on the result. Experiments on an srsRAN/Open5GS testbed showed trusted devices gained Level 2 access in 9 to 12 seconds, while untrusted devices were consistently denied promotion.

entry.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Images
entry.summary: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes Tripwire-WM, a framework for undetectable image watermarks that can both reject and report forgeries. It commits the generated image's semantics to the magnitudes of the initial latent noise, so forged images carry a watermark whose commitment does not match their content and are flagged as forged. Built on the PRC watermark and Gaussian Shading++, the method is said to preserve their undetectability.

entry.title: How Users Perceive Deceptive Design in In-Vehicle Infotainment Interfaces
entry.summary: User Perceptions of Deceptive In-Vehicle Infotainment User Interfaces arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies dark patterns, interface designs that steer users toward unfavorable choices, in in-vehicle infotainment systems built on Android Automotive OS. Researchers audited four automaker emulators and identified 17 dark-pattern types, then ran two user studies comparing implementations and measuring perceptions before and after a tutorial. They find a sophistication paradox: subtler designs are less likely to raise suspicion, so oversight should assess specific implementations rather than just presence.

entry.title: Modeling Mutable State Across Sessions in Security Protocol Analysis
entry.summary: Mutable State in Enrich-by-Need Security Protocol Analysis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses security protocols in which a principal keeps mutable state that restricts what its local sessions may do and that other local sessions can change. The authors show how to represent this cross-session mutable state within the strand space approach to symbolic protocol analysis. They implement the ideas in the Cryptographic Protocol Shapes Analyzer (CPSA). The core theory consists of two axioms characterizing state plus protocol-specific rules, which yield precise characterizations of protocol behavior in relevant cases and support the design of correct protocols that rely on such state.

entry.title: PriTabICL: Privacy-Protected Table Learning via Task-Aligned Cluster-Wise Data Synthesis
entry.summary: PriTabICL: Differentially Private Tabular In-Context Learning with Task-Aligned Cluster-Wise Synthesis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses privacy risks in tabular in-context learning, where large language models predict from a few labeled examples that may contain sensitive personal data. The authors propose PriTabICL, a framework compatible with existing differential privacy synthesis methods, which partitions records into private clusters, synthesizes each separately, and prioritizes feature-target relationships relevant to prediction. At inference, queries are routed to a cluster and demonstrations are sampled from its synthetic data. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that PriTabICL-PrivSyn beats global PrivSyn in 8 of 12 settings and outperforms existing private TabICL approaches in nearly all evaluated settings.

entry.title: Attacks and defenses in decentralized multi-agent systems where agents split and hand off tasks to each other
entry.summary: Attacks and Defenses in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems with Hop-by-Hop Task Decomposition and Delegation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies security threats posed by malicious agents in decentralized multi-agent LLM systems, where independently run agents decompose tasks and delegate work to peers. The authors design and evaluate attacks on integrity, availability, and confidentiality. They also present a cryptographic protocol that produces irrefutable verified execution traces, and an auditor that analyzes these traces to detect and attribute malicious behavior.

entry.title: Ties at the Top: Comparing CVSS and EPSS at a Fixed Budget
entry.summary: Ties at the Top: A Point-in-Time Comparison of CVSS and EPSS at a Fixed Budget arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a method for comparing vulnerability-prioritization strategies when only a fixed number of CVEs can be selected from a common eligible population. Using CVEs published in the NVD in 2025 and Q1 2026, it reconstructs scores and status 30 days after publication and compares CVSS and EPSS at a 5% budget against later KEV additions. The results show that tie-breaking among equal CVSS scores and the provenance of scores strongly affect outcomes, so fixed-budget comparisons should report their cutoff, eligible population, score sources, and tie-breaking rules.

entry.title: Stealing exact private training data from other clients in federated learning
entry.summary: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an attack pipeline in which a malicious client uses model updates from federated learning to reconstruct other clients' private text. The method iteratively subtracts the gradient contributions of sentences already recovered exactly, exposing the remaining sentences for recovery in later rounds. The authors report the first exact sentence recovery with 100% precision, recovering up to 80.2% of client sentences exactly on aggregates with up to 4 times more tokens than the model's hidden dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a new iterative attack unwinding FedAvg gradient entanglement, recovering up to 80.2% of client sentences exactly.

entry.title: Playing the SMR Game with Existential Honesty: a study of keeping blockchain consensus safe when no validator is guaranteed honest
entry.summary: Playing the SMR Game with Existential Honesty arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies state machine replication when every validator is rational or Byzantine and none is honest. It assumes one unidentified, always-online full node is honest, and clients relay certificates to full nodes and wait before confirming transactions. Under this setup, the protocol is always safe for any validator strategy, and the paper tightly characterizes how much transaction censorship a bribing adversary can achieve. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build an always-safe finalization layer for rational-Byzantine validators using certificate relay and an honest full node, and give a tight characterization of censorship.

entry.title: When Shuffling Fails: Recovering Tokens from Obfuscated KV Caches
entry.summary: When Shuffling Fails: Token Recovery from Obfuscated KV Caches arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines a shuffled obfuscation scheme for protecting KV caches in LLM serving. It shows that repeated input tokens make outputs indistinguishable, so the effective state space is about b rather than the claimed b! permutations. The authors present Repeat-to-Reveal, an attack that recovers an equivalent denoiser without the defender's secret parameters and can passively recover token multisets within a secret epoch. They evaluate it against KV-Cloak and other defenses. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show repeated tokens collapse the permutation state space from b! to b, enabling token recovery; the abstract reports experiments on KV-Cloak across nine models and 3,000 prompts.

entry.title: Plug-and-play watermarking that traces leaked Mixture-of-Experts LLM copies to individual licensees
entry.summary: Plug-and-Play Multi-Licensee Robust Watermarking for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents PPMoE, the first plug-and-play watermarking framework for Mixture-of-Experts large language models that supports multiple licensees. It trains compact, mergeable weight modules that steer the MoE router toward distinct, compatible routing patterns, so licensee-specific watermarks can be embedded at distribution time without retraining. The authors report high attribution accuracy under white-box and black-box threat models, with base model utility preserved and robustness against adaptive removal attacks across five MoE models and seven datasets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose mergeable incremental modules steering MoE routers for multi-licensee watermarking, reporting validation on five MoE models and seven datasets under white- and black-box attributio

entry.title: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Barriers to Stopping Elder Fraud on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
entry.summary: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies online discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba about older adults who keep trusting scammers, and the obstacles families face when trying to intervene. Using a mixed-methods analysis of 13,082 Reddit posts and 3,933 Baidu Tieba posts, it finds that older adults often resisted or stayed involved after being warned. Relatives frequently lacked legal authority to act without the victim's consent, and recovery of funds was very limited.

entry.title: LLM-guided identification of cyber-physical attack paths in smart grids
entry.summary: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a physics-grounded framework that uses large language models to identify cyber-physical attack paths in power systems, using cascading-failure impact rankings as reference. The framework combines system topology with LLM-guided STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK threat modeling and is compared against topology-driven, threat-driven, and fusion-based baselines. Structured LLM threat modeling substantially improves alignment with the physics-based references, and in the IEEE 14-bus system it reduces runtime by roughly 75 to 85 percent compared with the fusion-based baseline.

entry.title: Model Input Versus Model Limits: Checking Whether Language Models Know the Machine State Before Judging Industrial Commands
entry.summary: The Limit Is in the Input, Not the Model: State-Dependent Command Safety in Natural-Language Interfaces to Industrial Controllers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether language models judging commands to industrial controllers receive the current machine state needed for safety decisions. The same command can require opposite answers depending on state, so errors may stem from missing input rather than weak reasoning. The authors propose an answerability audit that pairs each command with two states requiring opposite answers and counts a pair only when both answers are correct. In a self-built test of 15 pairs, models without state could not reliably distinguish the cases, while adding state raised correct pairs in some models, ranging from 0 to 13 of 15.

entry.title: Gradient-based defensive poisoning against system identification attacks on cyber-physical systems
entry.summary: Gradient-Based Defensive Poisoning Against System Identification Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses AI-driven attacks that learn cyber-physical system (CPS) models by passively observing controller and plant signals. The authors inject small perturbations into the measurements an attacker observes to degrade neural-network-based system identification. The perturbations are derived from input gradients of several identification models and concentrated in transient regimes. On a simulated DC motor networked control system, they produce larger prediction errors than random poisoning of equal magnitude, and the signals also degrade N4SID-based identification.

entry.title: Lightweight, Robust Histogram Estimation Under Local Differential Privacy and the Effect of Dropout Attacks
entry.summary: Robust, Lightweight Locally Differentially Private Histogram Estimation and the Role of Dropout Attacks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses malicious clients manipulating outputs in local differential privacy by proposing a lightweight three-message verification framework. It uses proofs of plaintext evaluation to limit manipulation to selective dropout. Mean per-client latency stays below 500 milliseconds for PI-RAPPOR and Hadamard Response, and the authors give error bounds plus server-side consistency checks that need no client-side cryptography.

entry.title: SCR: Detecting Poisoned Training Samples via Clean-Reference Residuals
entry.summary: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes Semantic Counterfactual Residualization (SCR), a method that uses a small set of clean reference samples to reconstruct each sample's features and separate benign variation from poisoning signals. It detects backdoor-poisoned samples by finding coherent deviations from these clean baselines, without prior knowledge of the attack. Tested on twelve dirty-label and clean-label attacks across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet, SCR reports attack-averaged true positive rates above 99.5% and false positive rates below 2%, outperforming eight baseline detectors in macro-TPR.

entry.title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
entry.summary: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces RECLAIM, a training-free defense that protects vision-language-action robot policies from adversarial patches at inference time. It uses the frozen model's attention responses to local visual edits as feedback to decide where and how to purify the image, combined with robot geometry, and rechecks these choices as the scene changes during manipulation. Evaluated on patches from four attack methods across several manipulation task suites, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of tasks and raises LIBERO-Object success from 0% to 70.0%. Its mean decision time is 548.9 ms per control step.

entry.title: Testing coding agents' overeager actions in realistic sessions using continuation audits
entry.summary: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces Continuation Audits, a method that starts from a prefix of a real coding-agent session and has an auditor model continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour. On SWE-Chat prefixes, a judge could not reliably distinguish the continuations from their source sessions, and verbalized eval-awareness did not exceed the rate in unaudited real sessions. Applied to three recent models, each model led a different seed behaviour, and Kimi K3 kept bypassing file-permission protections after an explicit prohibition.

entry.title: Reducing fix reversal in function-level vulnerability detection with counterfactual constraints
entry.summary: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines function-level vulnerability detectors that rate fixed code as more vulnerable than the original, a problem called fix reversal, which it traces mainly to a function-length shortcut. The authors propose CFVul, using sliding-window encoding, a content constraint during training, and a length constraint averaging over reference lengths at inference. On PrimeVul, CFVul reaches a PairRank of 59.4%, exceeding the compared methods.

entry.title: Drift-aware explainable triage ranking of Windows malware files with semantic consistency checks
entry.summary: Drift-Aware Explainable Prioritization for Windows PE Malware Forensic Triage with Semantic Consistency Checks arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a framework for forensic triage of Windows PE malware that uses only pre-extracted static features and never executes the malware. A calibrated maliciousness score sets each file's priority, and per-sample feature attribution explains the prediction. The framework also checks whether top attributed features agree with behaviors documented in MBC and MITRE ATT&CK, and uses conformal evaluation and distribution tests to flag drift.

entry.title: PIPETTE: A Purple-Teaming Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in LLM Agents
entry.summary: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 18, 2026LLM agents that process untrusted external data are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks that hijack them into executing attacker-chosen tasks. The paper finds that two state-of-the-art RL-based red-teaming methods, RL-Hammer and PISmith, suffer from mode collapse, repeatedly finding similar attacks that do not improve robustness after adversarial training. The authors propose PIPETTE, which uses a dictionary learning-based reward to broaden attack coverage and an on-policy adversarial training pipeline for injection defense. Evaluations on AgentDojo and ASB show near-zero attack success rates on static attacks, resistance to strong adaptive attacks, and benign task utility close to the undefended baseline.

entry.title: AutoPI: A Red-Teaming Method That Tests LLM Agents for Prompt Injection Across Many Attack Types
entry.summary: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces AutoPI, an adaptive red-teaming method for finding prompt injection weaknesses in LLM agents. It uses the PIAtlas taxonomy of injection techniques to guide attacks and measure how many different techniques succeed, not just the overall attack success rate. The method is black-box and training-free, and it was evaluated on AgentDojo and IPI Arena.

entry.title: Retained encrypted search with certified split joins (a paper on keeping encrypted search working after data edits)
entry.summary: Retained Encrypted Search with Certified Split Joins arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies how to keep encrypted search valid across data edits and worker replacement by separating computational validity from current release authority. It presents exact Hamming-distance search that allows at most one authorized decryption and decoding attempt per query preparation. Under stated assumptions, bounded adaptive privacy is reduced to ordinary Ring learning with errors (Ring-LWE). Local CPU experiments on 32,768 vectors of 512 bits report a median of 9.825 s for the 60-bit-join construction versus 12.159 s for an optimized full-source-modulus baseline, though these are local implementation results, not deployment or concrete-security claims.

entry.title: PMKPIR: Parallel Multi-Keyword Private Retrieval with Interleaved Batching for Boolean Queries
entry.summary: PMKPIR: Parallel Multi-Keyword PIR with Interleaved Batching for Private Boolean Retrieval arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes PMKPIR, a keyword private information retrieval scheme that lets users retrieve database entries tied to keywords while keeping their queries private. It uses the SIMD capability of BFV homomorphic encryption to introduce an interleaved batching method and an IBPIR design that matches multiple keywords in a single database traversal. A boolean query processing method is also added to support universal boolean computation and speed up boolean operations. Compared with state-of-the-art schemes, the paper reports reductions of up to 79.06% in query time, 75.00% in communication, 97.92% in storage, and 80.26% in peak memory.

entry.title: Does Rendering Text as Images Block Prompt Injection?
entry.summary: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines whether rendering untrusted documents as page images protects multimodal language models from indirect prompt injection, where hidden commands in a document hijack answers. The authors compared text and image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, testing marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement attacks. Rendering lowers attack success on average, but protection varies by model, attack type, and settings, so the authors conclude it offers only conditional protection.

entry.title: Erased but Recoverable: Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Erased but Recoverable: On the Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines how concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models can weaken or reverse after downstream fine-tuning with DreamBooth, LoRA, or Custom Diffusion. The authors find that fine-tuning preserves certain high-contribution attention heads with stable output subspaces and response magnitudes. They propose SHACE, which identifies these stability-critical heads and keeps their parameters unchanged during erasure. The method is reported to improve resistance to concept recovery across fine-tuning settings while maintaining suppression and non-target generation quality.

entry.title: A study on applying control-flow integrity to skill-based LLM agents
entry.summary: Guarding the Kingdom of Skill-Based Agents in the AI Dynasty of Computation: Control-Flow Integrity for Agent Skills arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper introduces SkillCFI, which brings control-flow integrity to procedural skills executed by large language model agents. A compiler derives both the agent's instructions and an executable contract from one skill, and a deterministic runtime enforcer admits tool requests only with trusted evidence while refusing unmediated channels such as inline scripts. In 770 sessions on eight self-written skills, all 240 violations were blocked before dispatch, normal tasks completed at nearly the same rate, and checking took about 2% of task time.

entry.title: PULSAR-V: I/O-Aware Post-Update Attestation for RISC-V
entry.summary: PULSAR-V: I/O-Aware Post-Update Attestation for RISC-V arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents PULSAR-V, an attestation architecture for RISC-V devices that checks whether a firmware image remains protected after an update is committed, not just whether the intended firmware was installed. It binds the authenticated update commit to the effective permissions and immutability of both the CPU's PMP/EPMP gate and the I/O policy governing DMA, sampled at commit time and at attestation. On a ZCU102 FPGA prototype, PULSAR-V rejects a device whose committed image was corrupted by a DMA write, and also rejects an intact device whose I/O policy left the image writable.

entry.title: PIVOT: A Watermark That Hides Multi-Bit Messages in LLM Text Without Changing Its Distribution
entry.summary: PIVOT: Distribution-Preserving Multi-BitWatermarking with Minimax-Optimal Scoring arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents PIVOT, a watermarking method that embeds multi-bit messages into text generated by large language models. It uses mirrored rank-interval sampling so that each message bit shapes token choice while every token's probability is kept exactly the same. The authors frame detection and message recovery as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem and prove finite-sample recovery guarantees. Experiments on two representative LLMs show that PIVOT reliably detects watermarks and recovers messages.

entry.title: Intent Contracts: Removing Tools from LLM Agents
entry.summary: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes intent contracts, an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. At each step the planner submits a short logged contract containing a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields, which code validates before a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and generates the tool call. The authors compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands on three AmPermBench task families. Contracts do not reduce unauthorized actions, and when the environment is ambiguous, state-changing conditions hit a wrong target in 40-49% of runs.

entry.title: Do decision models help LLM-driven network discovery?
entry.summary: When Do Decision Models Help LLM-Driven Network Discovery? arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies whether adding fast, non-generative decision models to validate commands improves network discovery, the first phase of penetration testing, when it is automated by large language models. Using a simulation calibrated on a 30-node containerized testbed, it compares networks of 10, 100, and 1,000 hosts. Chunked batch dispatch recovers 92% to 100% of open ports at large scale, while single-host dispatch falls below 6%. Decision gating raises the local model's port recall from 75.5% to 89.0% on small networks and intercepts costly decoy tarpits, but adds latency for frontier models during early host discovery.

entry.title: Smoothing and learning to make RSS-based spoofing detection robust to movement
entry.summary: Smoothing and Learning for Movement-Robust RSS-Based Spoofing Detection arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies physical-layer spoofing detection, which uses received signal strength measured at several receivers to check whether transmissions claiming one identity come from different locations. It modifies an existing scheme by applying median or Gaussian temporal filtering to position-change detector scores and replacing the fixed threshold with a supervised classifier. On real indoor measurements from 52 transmitter locations, Gaussian filtering improves detector accuracy. The best classifier, XGBoost, reaches 0.949 accuracy and 0.940 F1 on a synthetic held-out test set, though it misses about a third of attacks where two transmitters move simultaneously.

entry.title: Weighing the Envelope: How Component Weight and Arbitration Shape Envelope-Layer Defenses for a Single LLM Agent
entry.summary: Weighing the Envelope: Component Weight and Arbitration in Envelope-Layer Defenses for a Single LLM Agent arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how malicious content enters a single LLM agent through the envelope layer, assuming an attacker pre-plants a malicious tool and poisons long-term memory that a benign request inadvertently triggers. It measures how labels, memory, tool roles, and the backend affect invocation decisions. The authors find that envelope labels act as a measurable, reversible weight rather than a switch, constrained by backend and tool role. They conclude such labels should serve as a soft gate within a broader defense, not replace permissions, sandboxing, or human review.

entry.title: PoCoFL: A policy-compliant federated learning framework that verifies client and aggregator behavior
entry.summary: PoCoFL: A Framework for POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning arXiv · Oct 3, 2026Federated learning keeps training data local, but it does not ensure that client contributions follow policy or that aggregators process admitted contributions correctly. The paper presents PoCoFL, which separates FL type, policy semantics, and cryptographic realisation. Clients prove compliance using commitments and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs, and aggregators prove they applied the chosen aggregation policy. The framework is demonstrated through vanilla, continual, personalised, and threshold-encrypted FL, with proof-of-concept implementations and evaluation of policy enforcement effects.

entry.title: Four Ciphers in One: Full-Round Attacks on the LLBC Reference Implementation
entry.summary: Four Ciphers in One: Full-Round Attacks on the Reference Implementation of LLBC IACR ePrint · Nov 15, 2026LLBC is a 128-bit low-latency block cipher for IoT, proposed in 2025. This paper finds that its released reference implementation differs from the published specification in eight points, including rotation amounts. The authors show the implementation splits into four independent 32-bit ciphers and attack all 20 rounds, decrypting on a single PC in 175.5 seconds. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show the reference implementation deviates from the specification, splits into independent ciphers, and report full 20-round attacks.

entry.title: Error bounds for Falcon's fast Fourier sampler under fixed-point arithmetic
entry.summary: Bounds of Falcon's Fast Fourier Sampler with Fixed-Point Arithmetic IACR ePrint · Nov 16, 2026This paper bounds the Rényi divergence between Falcon's fast Fourier sampler in real arithmetic and its fixed-point implementation, on the tail-cut event. It gives resulting security bit levels for n=512 at λ=128 and n=1024 at λ=256 over 2^64 signatures. The authors propose four changes to the fixed-point implementation, with proofs partly machine-checked in CryptoLine and Lean. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound Rényi divergence for Falcon's fixed-point sampler and propose four implementation changes, backed by machine-checked proofs and three code-alignment hypotheses.

entry.title: Communication-efficient threshold-CKKS secure aggregation for cross-silo federated learning
entry.summary: Communication-Efficient Threshold-CKKS Aggregation for Secure Cross-Silo Federated Learning IACR ePrint · Nov 15, 2026This paper proposes a threshold-CKKS homomorphic encryption protocol for cross-silo federated learning that requires no trusted key-distribution center. It offers Full and Sparse profiles, supporting server-side weighting and dropout-aware reaggregation, and reduces communication through seeded ciphertext reconstruction, selective coefficient transmission, and compressed collective decryption. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 show that Sparse substantially lowers online communication compared with FedPHE at matched accuracy, narrowing the communication gap between encrypted and plaintext federated learning.

entry.title: LEASH: When LaBRADOR's Guarantees Go Astray
entry.summary: LEASH: When LaBRADOR’s Guarantees Go Astray IACR ePrint · Nov 15, 2026This paper revisits the correctness and security analysis of LaBRADOR, a lattice-based succinct proof system. The authors construct explicit counterexamples showing its parameter-selection strategy can fail completeness even for valid binary R1CS witnesses. They also identify inconsistencies in recursive relation transformations and inaccuracies in knowledge-extraction probability bounds, and offer targeted repairs with mathematical analysis.

entry.title: Aker: An Efficient Two-Party Protocol for Distributed SLH-DSA Signing
entry.summary: Aker: Efficient Two-Party SLH-DSA IACR ePrint · Nov 15, 2026This paper presents Aker, a maliciously secure two-party signing protocol for SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), the NIST stateless hash-based signature standard, producing signatures that an unmodified FIPS 205 verifier accepts. It combines generic secret-sharing MPC with four optimizations exploiting the SLH-DSA hypertree, including concurrent evaluation of layers, cached public keys, reused upper-layer signatures, and locally sampled one-time subtrees. The authors implement the protocol with a GPU engine for server-to-server deployments, where SLH-DSA-128f online signing takes 2.09 seconds.

entry.title: Modular Walsh rigidity for degree-four Boolean functions
entry.summary: Modular Walsh rigidity for Boolean functions of degree at most four IACR ePrint · Nov 16, 2026The paper studies Boolean functions of degree at most four. It proves that such a function on 4m variables (m≥4, M=2^m) is bent if all its Walsh coefficients are congruent to ±M² modulo a single odd integer p≥9M/16. This improves the earlier sufficient bound p>7M/12 and includes the case M=16, p=9.

entry.title: Bit-by-bit Bleichenbacher oracle attack using partial message knowledge
entry.summary: A Bleichenbacher bit-by-bit oracle attack from partial message knowledge IACR ePrint · Nov 16, 2026This paper shows how an attacker who knows a few least significant bytes of an RSA message can use a server with an oracle side channel to decrypt the full message bit by bit. It considers two chosen-ciphertext oracles: one revealing whether the decrypted message starts with 00 02, and one revealing whether it is fully PKCS compliant. With the three least significant bytes known, the attack needs a small number of oracle calls. The method is also adapted to extract the few least significant bytes at higher cost.

entry.title: Rented Oscillations: Attacks and Defenses for Synchronized Workloads in Shared Data Centers
entry.summary: Rented Oscillations: Multi-Tenant Data Center Workload Synchronization Attacks and Mitigation arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a stealthy attacker who rents computing capacity in a multi-tenant data center and runs deliberately unoptimized large language model training, synchronizing many workloads into large periodic power oscillations. Each workload remains individually hard to distinguish from benign training. The authors characterize the periodicity experimentally, use a hardware-grounded threat model supported by supercomputer experiments, and identify oscillatory weak points in the network. They propose signal-energy-based detection and a mitigation that re-times workloads to reduce oscillatory energy, validated with power hardware-in-the-loop experiments and real-time simulations on a surrogate model of the Saudi Arabian transmission network. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a stealthy attack synchronizing rented data center workloads into periodic oscillations, with detection and re-timing mitigation validated on PHIL experiments and a Saudi grid surro

entry.title: ACaM: Automated capability modeling to find hidden dangers in AI agent tools
entry.summary: ACaM: Automated Capability Modeling for Agentic AI Security arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper addresses agentic AI systems, where tools can hide dangerous behavior that their natural-language descriptions do not mention, a gap it calls Description-Code Inconsistency. It proposes ACaM, a neurosymbolic method that derives each tool's capabilities from its code using static analysis, compiling agent source code into a capability property graph to reconstruct threat chains across multiple tool calls. Evaluated on 43 real-world agents, ACaM reports 98.3% macro-F1 on capability properties for 24 annotated agents and discovers hundreds of structural vulnerabilities, ten confirmed with proof-of-concept exploits. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose code-grounded capability modeling against description-code inconsistency, evaluated on 43 real agents with ten confirmed proof-of-concept exploits.

entry.title: BMuSig-L: a lattice-based blind multi-signature scheme
entry.summary: BMuSig-L: Blind Multi-Signature from Lattice IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents BMuSig-L, a two-round, concurrently secure blind multi-signature scheme based on lattices. A blind multi-signature lets a user obtain a joint signature from a group of signers while keeping the message hidden from them and preventing colluding signers from linking the signature to its signing session. The construction builds on MuSig-L, a concurrently secure lattice blind signature scheme, and a knowledge-sound non-interactive argument system. The authors prove one-more unforgeability under stated assumptions and present a prototype evaluating signature size and verification time.

entry.title: Concrete quantum circuits and resource estimates for quantum 3- and 4-sieves
entry.summary: Concrete Quantum Circuit Implementations and Resource Estimates for the Quantum 3 and 4-Sieves IACR ePrint · Nov 15, 2026This paper provides the first complete reversible quantum circuits for the quantum 3- and 4-sieve algorithms for the Shortest Vector Problem, proposed by Chailloux and Loyer in 2023. It designs inner-product predicates in three architectures (low-qubit, balanced, low-depth) and verifies them with exact state-vector simulations. The authors find that the original amplitude-amplification oracle fails when inner Grover searches are approximate, and they correct it. Applying their arithmetic techniques to the published NV 2-sieve oracle reduces its T-count and T-depth substantially.

entry.title: Slice Isolation-as-a-Service: A Mechanism for Proactively Defending Against Cross-Slice Attacks in 5G-Advanced and Beyond
entry.summary: Slice Isolation-as-a-Service: An Isolation Mechanism to Proactively Defend Cross-Slice Attacks in 5G-Advanced and Beyond arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper addresses security risks in network slicing for 5G-Advanced and 6G networks, proposing a Slice Isolation-as-a-Service framework that offers data plane isolation as an on-demand capability. The authors formulate multi-UPF resource allocation as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) problem and validate it on a containerized 5G testbed built with Free5GC and Nokia Containerlab. According to the paper, shared and VNF-only isolation fail under volumetric flooding and GTP-in-GTP reflection attacks, while MINLP-driven strict physical isolation neutralizes cross-slice injection and preserves 99.999% reliability for mission-critical slices.

entry.title: DetectViT: Detecting Backdoors in Vision Transformers at Test Time Using Attention Across Heads
entry.summary: DetectViT: Test-time Backdoor Detection for Vision Transformers via Inter-Head Attention Discrepancy arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Vision Transformers are widely used as visual encoders in multimodal models, but pretrained checkpoints from third parties can be vulnerable to backdoor attacks. This paper analyzes how backdoor triggers change the multi-head attention of ViTs and proposes DetectViT, a test-time detection method that uses inter-head consistency and entropy variance scores. The method needs only a small out-of-distribution calibration set and reuses attention weights already computed during inference, adding negligible overhead.

entry.title: Expressiveness and Convertibility of Rule-Based Access Control Policies
entry.summary: Expressiveness and Convertibility of Rule-Based Access Control Policies arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a systematic approach to study the semantics and compare the expressiveness of rule-based access control models, such as attribute-based access control, built on different rule structures and rule composition choices. It also examines whether a policy can be converted from one rule-based model to another, which matters for policy migration. The main results cover well-formedness properties of policy semantics, an expressiveness hierarchy among models, and the computational complexity of policy convertibility.

entry.title: JITAtlas: Checking Object Lifetime and Ownership in Compiler Rewrites
entry.summary: JITAtlas: Checking Lifetime and Protection Obligations in Compiler Rewrites arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper presents JITAtlas, a source-level checker that detects compiler rewrites which keep returned values correct but break object lifetime, borrowed-pointer support, or caller-visible ownership. On a 58-input benchmark labeled independently of the tool, it detects all 29 defects with no false reports on 29 safe inputs, outperforming PyRefcon and CpyChecker. Across three CPython snapshots it reports 194 violations, of which manual review confirms 92 (47.42% precision), and it finds 15 new bugs with reproducible proofs of concept.

entry.title: Data poisoning attacks on locally private triangle counting
entry.summary: Data Poisoning Attacks to Locally Differentially Private Triangle Counting Protocols arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines how malicious users can use data poisoning to distort triangle counts in graph analytics under local differential privacy (LDP). The authors analyze attack surfaces of both non-interactive and interactive LDP triangle counting protocols and propose a unified gain-driven attack framework. Experiments on four real-world graph datasets show these attacks significantly distort estimates, and existing defenses are shown to be insufficient.

entry.title: Genus-two superspecial curves over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational kernels
entry.summary: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies superspecial genus-two curves over prime fields and the rational (2,2)-isogenies between their Jacobians, which form the graph underlying isogeny-based cryptography. It classifies the Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points into eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on p, and a count of rational (2,2)-kernels. Closed formulas for the masses of the curves and kernels are given in terms of class numbers and a zeta value, and they agree with exact enumeration for 37 primes.

entry.title: JEV vs. LLMs: Comparing Models for Phishing Email Detection
entry.summary: JEV vs. LLMs: A Comparative Analysis for Phishing Email Detection arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper compares Jev 1.13, a typed decision model from TypeSafe AI, with three large language models on 1500 labelled emails for phishing detection. It evaluates classification accuracy, decision latency, token use, API cost, and probability calibration. Jev scored best on the reported accuracy, precision, recall, F1, speed, token count, cost, and calibration metrics. The authors suggest it is promising for fast, high-volume triage, but all four systems need further validation before standalone deployment.

entry.title: FlowSH: Detecting Web Attacks by Linking Unusual Network Flows with Server Logs
entry.summary: FlowSH: Detecting Web Attacks by Correlating Anomalous Network Flows and Endpoint Logs arXiv · Nov 18, 2026FlowSH is a system for detecting web attacks whether or not the traffic is encrypted with HTTPS. Instead of decrypting packets in transit, it correlates network flow metadata (NetFlows) with server-side logs, which contain decrypted payloads. It uses unsupervised machine learning to flag anomalous NetFlows and Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) similarity search over logs to confirm attacks. In a testbed with multiple web scanners, it detected 70% of SQL injection attacks that ModSecurity missed.

entry.title: An AI system that detects and sorts web injection attacks to protect web applications
entry.summary: Protecting Web Applications using a Multimodal AI-based System for Classifying Web Injection Attacks arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a multimodal AI system that detects and classifies web injection attacks against web applications. It uses unsupervised machine learning to flag anomalous network flows, then analyses web server logs with natural language processing and supervised learning to classify attacks. A similarity search engine based on locality sensitive hashing validates the classifications. Evaluated on eight attack classes, it achieved an F1 score of 91% and an accuracy of 95%.

entry.title: A-Tag: Cryptographic File Tagging That Proves a Live Human Was Present
entry.summary: A-Tag: Cryptographic File Tagging with Enforced Live Human Presence arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents A-Tag, a system that cryptographically binds a digital file to proof that a live human was present when the file was tagged. Liveness is checked using micro-motion signals shaped by human motor control, and the resulting tag is publicly verifiable and transferable. The authors formalize security properties, define an adversarial model including automated and relay attacks, and implement the system on commodity devices. They report over 99 percent recovery success for image-based artifacts and sub-second verification.

entry.title: Lossless reversible watermarking for authenticating AI-generated images
entry.summary: Lossless Reversible Watermarking for AIGC with Applications in Authentication arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies lossless reversible watermarking, which lets an image be exactly restored to its original watermarked version after permissible distortions. It combines the low entropy of the information needed for image generation with robust latent-space watermarking to preserve enough information for lossless recovery. To resist adaptive adversaries, it adds cryptographic message authentication, and the recovered image serves as reference evidence for a chosen analyzer to make the authentication decision. Experiments on Stable Diffusion show exact recovery under a wide range of distortions.

entry.title: Image watermarks that track revisions across reissues
entry.summary: Image Watermarking With Memory Across Reissuance arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper introduces reissuable provenance, which determines whether an image is current, superseded, or unissued and recovers the last authorized revision of each region. It proposes Generational Stratigraphy Fields (GSF), which combine watermark evidence with an authenticated live reference to the current release so that circulated copies need not be rewritten. In evaluation across 480 reissuance histories, GSF reports 99.67% accuracy in classifying issued images as current or superseded and 94.09% recall of unissued edits.

entry.title: A survey of operations methods for reinforcement learning training of large language models
entry.summary: A Survey on RLOps for Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents a systematic survey of RLOps, the methods for managing the efficiency and reliability of reinforcement learning training for large language models. The authors organize existing approaches into five stages: training setup, experience collection, reward computation, policy optimization, and model evaluation, and examine each stage's operational concerns and techniques. The survey also identifies open challenges such as training observability, cross-stage coordination, multi-run management, and RLOps for recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Asymmetric optical image watermarking: a two-layer image watermark using optical Fourier processing
entry.summary: Asymmetric Optical Image Watermarking arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a two-layer image watermark whose core Fourier transform is performed by a coherent optical 4F unit. The first layer binds an Ed25519 signature to the image content via Fourier magnitudes, so anyone with the public key can verify it offline. The second layer is a key-defined carrier written by a secret phase hologram and read by a matched-filter correlator. The work is evaluated by scalar-diffraction simulation, with no hardware built.

entry.title: Auditing State Transfers in Long-Running LLM Agents
entry.summary: Securing and Auditing Long-Horizon LLM Agents: State-Transfer Auditing and Controls in the Agent Harness arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines long-horizon LLM agents, which move state among working context, session history, persistent memory, and external environments through an execution harness. It proposes a state-transfer audit architecture that emits hash-chained records at each transfer boundary, combining deterministic and model-based semantic checks. The authors argue these records support both causal failure attribution and runtime security controls such as least-privilege capabilities and transactional recovery. A reference harness middleware was evaluated on 240 multi-step fault-injection trajectories, where it localized root causes and caught cross-transfer violations missed by conventional logs.

entry.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Training for Software Developers: A Literature Review
