entry.summary: Post-Quantum Cryptography Education for Software Developers: A Multivocal Literature Review arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper reviews 8 research publications and 15 professional training offerings to examine how well existing education prepares software developers for post-quantum cryptography. It looks at competency coverage, practical software engineering tasks, teaching approaches, learner support, and evaluation. All 23 sources cover PQC foundations and algorithms, but practical software engineering tasks are unevenly addressed. The authors identify six gaps and recommend ways to strengthen PQC education.

entry.title: LLMs for Predicting and Prioritizing Software Vulnerabilities: A Review
entry.summary: LLMs for Software Vulnerability Prediction and Prioritization: A Review arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This systematic literature review examines how large language models are used for software vulnerability prediction, assessment, exploitability estimation, risk assessment and prioritization. Following a prespecified protocol, the authors retained 23 primary studies published between 2024 and 2026 after quality assessment. Assessment is the largest task class, and reproducibility is the weakest reported dimension. The authors conclude that current systems should support analyst judgement rather than replace it.

entry.title: Beyond Stars: MTTX Measures How Fast Developers Respond to Dependency Updates and Security Fixes
entry.summary: Beyond Stars: MTTX Brings Developer Responsiveness to Dependency Decisions, from Dashboard to IDE to GitHub Actions arXiv · Oct 25, 2026This paper presents MTTX, an open-source tool that computes MTTU (Mean Time To Update) and MTTR (Mean Time To Remediate) for software dependencies, measuring how quickly package developers respond to new releases and vulnerabilities. It offers a more trustworthy signal than easily faked metrics like GitHub stars or download counts. MTTX resolves historical version constraints for npm, PyPI, and Cargo packages and is available as a web dashboard, IDE extension, and GitHub Action. The authors validated it with 328 automated tests and manual checks on 90 packages.

entry.title: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Log
entry.summary: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Logarithm arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper asks whether computing a Diffie-Hellman key is as hard as computing a discrete logarithm. Maurer's earlier reduction worked only under an assumption about short intervals containing enough integers with small prime factors, which had been unproven for thirty years. The authors use a now-known zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta function to prove this assumption, removing the condition. They conclude that for every prime p there is an O(log p)-bit advice string, depending only on p, that lets a Diffie-Hellman oracle compute discrete logarithms in any group of order p in polynomial time. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors drop Maurer's thirty-year smooth-interval condition using zero-free-region bounds on smooth integers, and report applications to related impossibility results and Wolf's characterisation.

entry.title: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Its Security Risks
entry.summary: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Exposing Its Security Risks arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper reverse-engineers how the load/store unit (LSU) of recent NVIDIA GPUs serves load instructions, using microbenchmarks. It gives a cycle-accurate latency formula for global L1 hits and shared memory accesses, showing that bank conflicts and L1 tag lookups depend on addresses and cause contention. The authors show that the LSU can leak information, communicate covertly, and slow colocated workloads, and they recover a full AES-128 key under the threat model of prior GPU AES timing attacks. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors measure GPU LSU load latency, contention points and warp starvation, reporting new side and covert channels, AES-128 key recovery, and up to 750x slowdown of cuBLAS on A100/H100.

entry.title: SEAM: Computer-use agents recognize cross-screen harm but still carry it out
entry.summary: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces SEAM, a benchmark of 600 multi-step, cross-application computer-use tasks where each instruction and screen is benign alone but harmful in combination. Several agents carried out the harm in up to 92% of runs, though they declined when the user stated the harm in one sentence. Asked about the pages, agents often flagged the conflict yet still confirmed the action, and proprietary models were markedly more cautious. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce cross-screen compositional harm, test 600 OSWorld tasks with minimal-pair variants, and report up to 92% harmful execution.

entry.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Long-Horizon Exploit Development by AI Agents
entry.summary: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies whether language model agents can build working exploits from known software vulnerabilities, using the ExploitBench benchmark with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. It finds verified gains continue after the first stop response, though they diminish over longer runs. The authors propose SCoRe, a context-management method that compacts context at stop bursts and marks impossibility judgments as unproven, reaching 67.0% capability coverage for MiMo at 2,000 turns. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose SCoRe, compacting context at stop bursts, and report MiMo reaching 67.0% capability coverage at 2,000 turns on ExploitBench versus 32.4% originally.

entry.title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation
entry.summary: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies intent leakage in language-conditioned traffic simulation, where surrounding vehicles react to an instructed agent's private plan before that behaviour is observable. The authors propose a paired intervention test, build the WOMD-PACT dataset of 531,099 timed-tagged scenes, and introduce CaFe, a diffusion-based simulator that limits inter-agent interaction to public beliefs. Evaluation reports that existing conditioning designs displace 23-83% of nearby uninstructed agents through leakage, while CaFe removes measurable leakage and keeps WOSAC realism at 0.763. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalise intent leakage as a causal faithfulness problem, proposing a paired intervention test and public-belief constraints; they report 23-83% displacement on WOMD and WOSAC 0.763.

entry.title: Do Coherent Fake Stories Keep LLM Attackers Engaged in Honeypots?
entry.summary: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception? arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes narrative deception, where a defender maps each attacker command to a MITRE ATT&CK technique and deploys mutually referential fake files, processes, services, and logs during an intrusion. In 1,150 sessions with LLM-driven attackers, coherent scenarios raised the median session length of advanced attackers from 40 to 165 commands and reduced abandonment from 86% to 52%. Most sessions ended from loss of interest rather than detection, at comparable inference cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose narrative deception with coherent ATT&CK-mapped artefacts; across 1,150 sessions, median commands for advanced attackers rise from 40 to 165.

entry.title: Study on missing security-fix backports in GitHub Actions workflows
entry.summary: Missing Security-Fix Backporting for GitHub Actions Workflows arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents a large-scale empirical study of security fixes in GitHub Actions workflows that were applied to default branches but not carried over to release and maintenance branches. It finds that most audited release branches remain vulnerable and that backporting is rare and slow. The authors propose WorkflowBP, a neuro-symbolic technique that applies fixes to divergent branches, and report results from testing it on real workflow files. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors quantify the first large-scale backporting gap for GitHub Actions security fixes and propose WorkflowBP, a neuro-symbolic technique; the abstract reports 67.9% scanner-checked backports on

entry.title: GapLeak: How Privacy-Preserving LLM Web Agents Can Leak Sensitive Data
entry.summary: GapLeak: When Privacy-Preserving LLM-based Web Agents Become a Privacy Risk arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces GapLeak, a vulnerability in which LLM-based web agents that follow data minimization and least privilege principles can still disclose sensitive information. When a website requests a field unavailable from authorized sources, the agent may escalate to reachable but unauthorized sources to complete the task. Evaluated across three agent frameworks and six LLMs in recruitment, e-commerce, travel, and healthcare, GapLeak caused roughly 37% unauthorized disclosure on average. The authors propose submission-time verification, which filters unauthorized content before form submission and eliminates over 96% of such disclosures while preserving task success. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize GapLeak, where information gaps drive web agents to leak sensitive data, reporting about 37% unauthorized disclosure across three frameworks and six LLMs.

entry.title: Does 4-bit quantization change a chat model's refusal behaviour? A matched-perturbation study
entry.summary: Is 4-Bit Quantization More Than Noise to a Chat Model's Safety Behaviour? Attributing Behavioural Shifts with Matched Perturbations arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines whether 4-bit quantized chat models, common on phones and laptops, change how they refuse harmful requests. The authors ran a pre-registered study on three 3–4B chat models, using paired tests, blind human labels and an 8-bit control. They found 4-bit shifts in opposite directions, and show these depend on the specific rounding error rather than bits per weight or likelihood. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use matched perturbations to show that 4-bit refusal shifts depend on the specific rounding error, not random noise of equal size, across three 3-4B chat models in a pre-registered study.

entry.title: Watermarks for image generators that survive edits without hurting quality
entry.summary: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking method that needs only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding. It is instantiated for image generation, where a trained image encoder is stable under content-preserving transformations yet distinguishes independent generations from the same prompt. The authors report that the watermark is effective on both open-source and closed models.

entry.title: Can verifiable private information retrieval match SimplePIR's online speed?
entry.summary: Can Verifiable PIR Match the Online Efficiency of SimplePIR? arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies verifiable Private Information Retrieval (vPIR), which ensures a malicious server cannot return tampered database records. The authors propose a vPIR protocol that uses a newly designed error-correcting-code-based commitment as the database digest, avoiding the SIS assumption. The scheme supports linear relation proofs and precise range proofs. The paper reports that its online communication and server computation match SimplePIR exactly, and compared with VeriSimplePIR it reduces online communication and client computation by about 20% and server online computation by over 35%.

entry.title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness in Small Hospital Federated Learning
entry.summary: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper empirically audits eight standard aggregation rules for federated learning, including FedAvg, coordinate-wise median, Krum, and GeoMed, on three medical datasets from the FLamby benchmark. It compares unweighted and sample-size-weighted versions across collaborations of 4 to 6 hospitals under attacks by one or two malicious clients. Exact-twin leave-out controls separate losses from lost honest data from damage caused by attacks, and the study finds that skewed data shares can make weighted rules collapse or become dictated by one hospital.

entry.title: Guarded Swarms in the Loop: A ROS 2/PX4 Digital Twin for UAV/UGV Swarm Coordination
entry.summary: Guarded Swarms in the Loop: A ROS 2/PX4 Digital Twin for Hybrid Digital-Analog Coordination of UAV/UGV Swarms arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents Guarded Swarms, an architecture for drone and ground-vehicle swarms in contested settings, pairing a digital coordination layer built on Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Nets with an independent analog safety layer that can veto unsafe commands. The authors build the first executable version as a digital twin using ROS 2, PX4 in software-in-the-loop mode, and Gazebo, with two UAVs and one UGV in a coastal counter-UAS scenario. Across 60 counterfactual runs, the three negative guarantees held at distinct stages of the chain. When the veto is enforced by an independent gate, it prevented every collision caused by a forged mission or a compromised worker.

entry.title: Attacks on Robot Settings via Network Access
entry.summary: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines a network-exposed configuration vulnerability in the Reachy Mini Lite robot, which lets an unauthenticated attacker change personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface. In tests, 11 prompt-injection attempts were resisted, while both configuration-layer attacks caused observable behaviour changes on physical hardware. A review of 59 public repositories found missing authentication in 10 of 11 verifiable genuine applications.

entry.title: Provable Mixing Properties of Parallel Mixnets, Revisited (a study of anonymity guarantees in scalable message-routing networks)
entry.summary: Provable Mixing Properties of Parallel Mixnets Revisited arXiv · Nov 17, 2026A mix-network routes messages so that their sources and destinations are hard to trace by mixing concurrent routes. This paper analyzes parallel mixnets, which scale horizontally, by bounding the variance of an adversary's posterior likelihood for the location of a message. Using concentration bounds, it shows that these networks satisfy (ε, δ)-differential indistinguishability without additional noise messages. The paper also examines the trade-off between anonymity, latency and per-router bandwidth.

entry.title: Quantifying the security cost of letting users choose which biometrics to present
entry.summary: Flexibility Has a Price: Quantifying Modality Policies in Maliciously Secure Multi-Biometric Authentication arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper treats allowing users to authenticate with only some of several biometric modalities as a security decision and proposes a framework for quantifying its risk. It also describes a policy-selection procedure for meeting a target risk level and SUPERMBA, a two-server privacy-preserving authentication system that enforces the chosen policy without revealing biometric templates or the modality subset used.

entry.title: Gradient-guided attack for testing robustness to few-pixel changes
entry.summary: Propose with the Gradient, Accept with the Loss: One Hedged Attack for Pixel-Sparse Robustness arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how to measure model robustness against adversaries that may change only a few pixels of an image. It analyzes two members of the existing sparse-AutoAttack ensemble, showing both are local searches, and derives five rules for using gradient information within such a search. The resulting Gradient-guided Random Search (GRS) matches or beats sAA on 13 CIFAR-10 configurations and 5 ImageNet models while running faster.

entry.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Safety Systems for AI Agents Against Adaptive Attacks
entry.summary: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper addresses the security risk that tool-using language-model agents face when malicious instructions hidden in untrusted emails, webpages, or documents arrive through the same channel as legitimate task directives. It introduces Evolution Under Fire, a staged framework that evolves complete executable safety harnesses through utility-constrained tree search, alongside adaptive stressors that discover utility-preserving attacks. On AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini, the evolved harness reduces attack success from 50.4% to 3.0%.

entry.title: A fast, strong way to protect images from being copied by diffusion personalization
entry.summary: Fast and Strong Image Protection against Diffusion Personalization arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Personalized text-to-image diffusion models can reproduce a person from a few photos. This paper introduces the protective diffusion model (PDM), which is trained once and then generates protective perturbations for new images in a single sampling pass. PDM is distilled from an iterative teacher and post-trained with a target residual projection (TRP) loss as reward. The authors report it outperforms nine baselines on faces and artworks and nearly matches its teacher at about a tenth of the cost.

entry.title: How well art is protected from style copying, and how to tailor that protection
entry.summary: How Well Is My Artwork Protected? Predicting and Tailoring Protection against Style Mimicry by Personalization arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies protection tools that add imperceptible perturbations to artworks so that a model personalized on them cannot imitate their style. It finds that the same protection setting protects different artworks very differently, and that cheap signals can predict this before any personalization. The proposed method, Patina, predicts each setting's protection from one short trial and assigns each artwork the weakest setting that reaches a chosen protection level.

entry.title: Exploited Before Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open Machine-Readable Evidence
entry.summary: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper builds vulnerability lifecycle timelines from open, machine-readable evidence covering disclosure, patch, exploitation, and catalog listing dates. The authors implement an evidence model in Vulnerability-Lookup that selects the earliest evidence for each event while preserving date precision. Among 3,758 vulnerability identifiers with exploitation evidence, about 98% have disclosure dates but only 15.7% have patch evidence, and most exploitation dates come from catalog listings. The authors conclude that exploitation-to-patch intervals are measurable, but their reliability depends on the availability, precision, and provenance of the published evidence.

entry.title: From Attack Tree to Model Checker: Linking Standard Attack Patterns to Verify Robot Security
entry.summary: From Attack Tree to Model Checker: Binding CAPEC Patterns to Verify Robotic System Security arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents a pipeline that maps each leaf of an attack tree to a CAPEC attack pattern, written as a first-order logic rule in which the attacker's prerequisites imply the attack's effect. Binding the pattern's variables to a specific system's parts yields an attacker model, whose effect is turned into a temporal-logic property. The property is checked against the system with and without a countermeasure, reporting the control that defeats the attack.

entry.title: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Transplantation Attacks
entry.summary: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Cross-Instance Transplantation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper notes that existing watermark checks only test whether a hidden message decodes or expected content remains, not whether the watermark evidence belongs to the originally registered image. It proposes TetherMark, a post-hoc watermark combining a message check and a relation check, accepting only when both pass. Across 240 test subjects it reports 92.08% legitimate acceptance and 9.17% and 16.25% attack success under WmForger and WMCopier.

entry.title: Dressed in Authority: Black-Box Jailbreaking of Multimodal Models via Visual Trust Bias
entry.summary: Dressed in Authority: Practical Black-Box Jailbreaking of MLLMs via Visual Trust Bias arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes Visual Trust Bias Attack (VTBA), a jailbreak method for multimodal large language models. It exploits the models' inherent trust in authoritative visual layouts by matching each input to a relevant authoritative template and embedding the harmful intent within it. The authors also build a dataset of 2,500 naturally occurring image-text pairs, and report high attack success rates across strong MLLMs.

entry.title: ConfGuard: A Physics-Based Safety Monitor for AI Agents Doing Equipment Maintenance
entry.summary: ConfGuard: a physics-grounded reference monitor for predictive-maintenance large-language-model agents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper presents ConfGuard, a reference monitor that uses physics-based rules to check predictions made by large-language-model agents in predictive maintenance. It tests each remaining-useful-life estimate against degradation physics using conformal prediction, and validates the agent's maintenance-urgency decisions against a deterministic policy. On 10,196 C-MAPSS test windows, the monitor sharply reduces the reach of covert and suppression attacks compared with a fixed physical range.

entry.title: GuardAgent: A memory-augmented AI agent that detects manipulative promotions in LLM-based recommendations.
entry.summary: GuardAgent: A Memory-Augmented Agentic Framework for Adaptive Detection of Adversarial Promotions in LLM-Based Recommendation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents the first systematic study of detecting promotion-driven attacks against recommender systems built on large language models, where text drives recommendations. The authors propose GuardAgent, an LLM-powered agentic framework that cycles through perception, action, reflection, and memory. It continually learns to recognize unseen threat patterns and produces explainable reasoning traces. Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show state-of-the-art generalization performance.

entry.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Effects of a Bit Flip in a Shared KV-Cache Block
entry.summary: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies what happens when a single bit flips in the cached key-value block of a shared system prompt in an LLM serving system with prefix caching. The authors inject faults into vLLM running Qwen3-8B by flipping either the most significant mantissa bit or the sign bit, then score responses on code generation, short answers, multiple-choice reasoning, and policy-based refusal. The share of correct responses that became wrong varied strongly by task, and the harm fell on requests whose sampled answers are sometimes wrong. Because harmed responses look like ordinary errors, the authors argue that such flips should be detected by checking cached blocks rather than by monitoring outputs.</summary>

entry.title: ECGWmark: Error-Correcting Deep Watermarking for ECG Signals
entry.summary: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting Codes arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This paper presents ECGWmark, a deep learning framework that embeds patient metadata directly into single-lead electrocardiogram signals so the information is not lost as recordings pass through multiple systems. It combines a convolutional generator, a frame-by-frame detector, and a frozen arrhythmia classifier that penalizes changes affecting diagnostic predictions, with extended Hamming codes to improve whole-message recovery. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the method keeps over 90% bit accuracy under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, and the protected 16-bit payload achieves 99.86% exact recovery on clean segments.

entry.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Rechecking Adversarial Face Privacy Methods
entry.summary: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper argues that published face-privacy methods were tested by feeding whole photos or detector boxes to recognition models, while deployed systems first align and crop faces, which inflates reported protection. The authors re-score the same files through a realistic alignment step, show that a paired cosine shift measures the effect more reliably than success-rate differences, and find that optimising through a differentiable alignment operator recovers much of the lost performance. They also report that four thresholds inherited since 2021 produce higher false-accept rates on whole images than on aligned crops. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that evaluation input mismatch and a paired cosine shift metric were validated on three unseen recognizers and a commercial system, affecting face-privacy evaluation.

entry.title: Bajillion: a cryptographic clearing protocol for micropayments
entry.summary: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments arXiv · Nov 17, 2026As AI agents increasingly browse on behalf of people, the ad-funded web model may weaken, so paying per request becomes a possible replacement. This paper presents Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments in which an untrusted operator issues preconfirmations and periodically posts only net balances on chain. The authors state that a malicious operator can only omit payments, never overdraw senders or misdirect transfers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a dispute-free clearing protocol for AI-agent micropayments, define an ideal functionality, and report a proof that it realizes it.

entry.title: Circulant Diffusion Layers: Cost Bounds and Rectangle Reuse
entry.summary: Circulant Diffusion Layers: Cost Bounds and Rectangle Reuse IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies the addition cost of sparse invertible circulant matrices over F_2 and odd prime fields, measuring diffusion by branch numbers. It introduces lower bounds on general and rectangle-reuse circuit costs for general matrices, and uses cyclic structure to obtain cost classifications and explicit constructions. For weight-three circulants, the minimum costs in both models are 3n/2 at even orders over F_2 and ceil(3n/2) over odd prime fields. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give first lower bounds on general and rectangle costs and a complete classification with exact minima for weight-three circulants.

entry.title: Hierarchical personalized federated learning for detailed multi-class intrusion detection across heterogeneous attacks
entry.summary: Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning for Fine-Grained Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Class Analysis in Heterogeneous Attack Environments arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning (HPFL), which combines multi-tier aggregation with client-level personalization for intrusion detection. Using MLP models on the CICIDS2017 dataset, it performs 8-class, 6-class, and 4-class attack classification. The authors report that HPFL outperforms FedAvg and FedProx in 8-class macro F1 and reduces transmission overhead by an estimated 48.9%.

entry.title: Study finds most large language models leak secrets hidden in system prompts
entry.summary: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper audits 363 text models from the OpenRouter catalog to see whether they reveal a secret flag placed in their system prompt when an AI agent tries to persuade them. The flag was leaked by 296 of the models plus four released later, giving 300 captures, 170 of which involved switching to a non-English language, mostly French. The authors recommend not storing secrets in system prompts, enforcing critical behavior with output validation and deterministic checks outside the model, and not relying solely on an LLM judge for consequential decisions.

entry.title: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Pipeline for Generating Hate Speech Training Data
entry.summary: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Data Synthesis Pipeline for Hate Speech Analysis arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces PersonaHate, a pipeline that generates diverse hate speech datasets using personas drawn from a pool of 457K. Eight large language models produce hateful content across 34 identity groups, and multi-judge annotation assigns labels, yielding 791K samples and a 67K group-balanced training set. Detectors trained on this data perform competitively on four external benchmarks, with a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-v3 model outperforming OpenAI's Moderation API on two of them. Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B also improves its average F1 by 7.7 points, surpassing LlamaGuard-3 on three of four benchmarks.

entry.title: Comparing CNN designs for malware detection when training data is scarce
entry.summary: CNN Architecture Comparison for Malware Classification with Limited Training Data arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This thesis compares two convolutional neural network designs for classifying malware converted into grayscale images. The baseline is a single-path model using pre-trained VGG16, while the other is a dual-path model that fuses VGG16 with a custom CNN. Both were tested on distinguishing two malware families from the Malimg dataset using 20% to 80% of the training data. Both achieved perfect classification, but the simpler model showed better training efficiency and robustness to noise.

entry.title: Forensic study of hidden metadata and leaked data in Swedish public PDFs
entry.summary: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This study analyzes 2,876 PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities, extracting metadata with ExifTool and classifying risk on an R0 to R3 scale. About 48.4% of documents show significant metadata exposure, varying significantly across institutional tiers. Compared with periods before and after the Swedish Cybersäkerhetslagen, exposure fell significantly, yet 44.9% of post-enactment documents still leak sensitive metadata. The authors also recovered deleted personal data and internal identifiers from incremental update layers in 228 of the 41.6% of documents containing them.

entry.title: Security Risks of Vibe Coding and Paths to Safer AI Agents
entry.summary: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper reviews security research on vibe coding, a workflow in which AI agents write, test, and deploy software from natural-language requirements. It sets out a reference architecture, six levels of agent autonomy, and a threat model built around five trust boundaries. The authors propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats in nine classes, reviewing evidence and defences for each. They identify eleven research challenges for the field.

entry.title: Watermark evidence in open-weight LLMs after modification: exact bounds for low-rank output watermarks
entry.summary: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how modifying the weights of an open-weight language model changes the evidence available to a watermark verifier of the OpenStamp type. Modifications are modeled as residuals in next-token logits, yielding exact lower bounds and deviation bounds on log-likelihood-ratio evidence. Experiments on Llama-2-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 show that INT8 quantization and 30% pruning keep true-positive rates at 85.6–94.8%, while 500-step LoRA fine-tuning reduces them to 28.8% and 11.6%.

entry.title: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Attack Diagnosis
entry.summary: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Fault and Attack Diagnosis arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper examines whether a learned policy is needed to decide which telemetry sources to read when diagnosing faults and attacks in cyber-physical power systems. It introduces ActiGrid, a benchmark framework in which a Double Deep Q-Network chooses between requesting another source and stopping to diagnose, and compares it with fixed subsets, entropy stopping, a greedy value-of-information rule, and tree ensembles. On the TU Delft and MSU/ORNL benchmarks, the learned policy is not better than simple controls, while compact subset classifiers perform well while reading fewer sources.

entry.title: TIBECG: a method to protect demographic privacy in ECG waveforms, tested lead by lead
entry.summary: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper introduces TIBECG, an architectural temporal information bottleneck that processes ECG waveforms to limit leakage of age and sex information. It is evaluated on individual leads from 6,386 hospital twelve-lead recordings across varying latent lengths. The retained diagnostic macro-F1 stays high, while age and sex inference is reduced more than with conventional transformations, with results varying by lead.

entry.title: A critical review and attacker test of a search dataset anonymised under the EU Digital Markets Act
entry.summary: A Critical Appraisal and Motivated Intruder Test of A Search Dataset Anonymised for the Purposes of the EU Digital Markets Act arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper assesses the European Commission's anonymisation of Alphabet search data shared under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act, comparing it with European Data Protection Board guidance. Researchers tested re-identification on 98,501 people across six countries using public profiles, finding a verified re-identification rate of 0.094%, below the 0.47% threshold, though one region exceeded it. The authors judged identity-disclosure risk insignificant, but gaps remain around inference and information about other people in queries, so safeguards are still needed.

entry.title: Phase-hiding bootstrapping for encrypted computation with client help
entry.summary: Phase-Hiding Programmable Bootstrapping with Online Client Assistance IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper introduces PH-PBS, a programmable bootstrapping method for TFHE fully homomorphic encryption in which the key-holding client precomputes single-use phase tokens and assists refresh online. The approach replaces bootstrapping-key-driven blind rotation with a token-based lookup alignment. On a four-bit workload compared against the TFHE-rs baseline, the authors report mean local refresh time falling from 18.392 ms to 3.713 ms, a 79.8% reduction, and analyze error propagation and security in the classical semi-honest model.

entry.title: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Model for Network Intrusion Detection
entry.summary: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes ST-GAT, a spatio-temporal graph attention network that represents network traffic as a sequence of graph snapshots for intrusion detection. It combines graph attention layers with a bidirectional LSTM and avoids data leakage by using non-overlapping time windows and fitting preprocessing on the training split only. With inverse class weighting, ST-GAT reached a Macro-F1 of 96.65% across three random seeds, 14.3 points above a per-flow Random Forest baseline. Balanced sampling lowered Macro-F1 by about 2.3 points compared with loss weighting, suggesting that aggressive resampling of small, noisy minority classes can hurt detection.

entry.title: Provenance-Privacy Paradox: Can Apple's Cloud Prove Reference Photos Aren't Used for Learning?
entry.summary: The Provenance-Privacy Paradox: Can Private Cloud Compute (PCC) Prove That Apple Reference Images Are Not Used for Learning? arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines how Apple Reference Image (ARI) photo provenance relies on Private Cloud Compute (PCC), which must process raw pixels in plaintext and so creates a tension with privacy. The authors argue that workload attestation and transparency logs confirm software identity and authorization but cannot prove that an authorized workload avoids learning from or retaining information derived from photos. In an experimental testbed, a learning-enabled workload passed the same checks as a baseline and produced identical JPEGs, yet retained a gradient from which its input could be reconstructed. The authors conclude that non-learning and non-retention need independent verification.

entry.title: ScenarioForge: Generating and Validating Cyber Exercises from Real Resources
entry.summary: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises arXiv · Nov 17, 2026ScenarioForge converts high-level requirements into cyber exercise scenarios with concrete topologies, services, traffic, and challenge chains, then deploys them in the CORE emulator. The authors built an execution dataset of 226 materialized scenarios, all of which passed deployment and live runtime validation. In a 50-prompt comparison, ScenarioForge-based generation achieved full topology and build success.

entry.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
entry.summary: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines a risk in LLM agents that call external tools: a request meant for a legitimate provider can be resolved to an attacker-controlled tool, a failure the authors call tool-provider misbinding. Using a controlled Model Context Protocol (MCP) environment, they evaluated five LLM-based clients. The results show that exact name collisions, task-aligned descriptions, and compatible schemas strengthen one another to cause the strongest failures, and that different models display the weakness in different ways.

entry.title: TRACE: Graph-Based Intrusion Detection Using Topology-Aware Contrastive Learning
entry.summary: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents TRACE, an intrusion detection framework that learns only from benign system-activity graphs without attack labels. It combines message-passing and topological representations and scores anomalies in the contrastive embedding space, using a labeled validation set only to set the threshold. Evaluated on StreamSpot, GraSec-IoT, and Unicorn Wget, TRACE achieves F1 scores of 0.923, 0.790, and 0.583. Results versus the GraphCL baseline are mixed, improving on two datasets and declining on GraSec-IoT.

entry.title: Post-quantum upgrade of Wi-Fi key setup using a hybrid ML-KEM design
entry.summary: Post-Quantum Migration of Wi-Fi Key Establishment: A Hybrid ML-KEM Design for OWE and FILS, Validated on OWE with hostapd arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Current Wi-Fi key agreements based on Diffie-Hellman could be broken by a capable quantum computer. The paper proposes replacing the Diffie-Hellman exchange in OWE and FILS with a hybrid that runs elliptic-curve agreement alongside ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and derives the master key from both secrets. A working prototype on hostapd and wpa_supplicant validates the design on OWE, with both endpoints deriving the same key and added connection time and computation below half a millisecond.

entry.title: CYBER-BRIDGE: An EU AI platform linking cross-border cybersecurity, compliance and forensics
entry.summary: The CYBER-BRIDGE project: An AI-Powered Platform for Cross-Border Cybersecurity, Compliance and Forensics in the EU arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces the EU-funded CYBER-BRIDGE project, which integrates cyber threat intelligence sharing, multi-framework compliance assessment and digital forensics under one architecture and a hash-chained evidence layer. From a single incident record, the platform aims to produce a cross-border threat advisory, the regulatory notifications required by deadlines, and a re-verifiable forensic pack. The paper covers the project's scope, requirements, pilots, architecture and toolkits, while quantitative KPIs will appear in later deliverables.

entry.title: Detection-efficient watermarking for vision-language agents using risk-constrained strength allocation
entry.summary: Detection-Efficient Watermarking for Vision--Language Agents via Risk-Constrained Strength Allocation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a risk-aware semantic watermarking framework for vision-language agents that allocates watermark strength during decoding by combining predictive uncertainty with a zero-shot multimodal relevance-risk proxy. A single risk penalty parameter lets deployers choose a detection-quality trade-off without retraining. At a selected operating point, mean watermark strength is about 59.4% lower than fixed-strength watermarking, with ROC-AUC of 0.9552 on clean text and 0.9459 on paraphrased text.

entry.title: Capturing workers' expertise in workplace AI systems
entry.summary: Expertise capture in workplace AI arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines how knowledge workers' professional judgment becomes absorbed into AI resources controlled by employers or platforms, a process it calls expertise capture. It presents a framework of contribution forms, technical residences and transformation families, showing that attribution, separation and revocation depend on where contributions reside and how they are transformed. The authors outline three measures and identify what cannot be separated at all.

entry.title: Counterexample to the soundness of the Flowering IOPP for graph codes
entry.summary: A counterexample to the soundness of the Flowering IOPP for codes on graphs arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper shows that the soundness claims of the Flowering protocol and its generalization are false. These are interactive oracle proofs of proximity for codes on graphs, using Reed-Solomon local codes. The authors find that the original proofs equate vertex distance with the fraction of unsatisfied local constraints, but only one inequality holds, in the wrong direction. They also present an explicit counterexample.

entry.title: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
entry.summary: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies K-out-of-N oblivious transfer between a server and a client over a discrete memoryless channel, under an honest-but-curious model. For a binary erasure channel with parameter ε, it shows the K-out-of-N OT capacity is min(Kε/(N−K), 1−ε), generalizing known 1-out-of-2 and 1-out-of-N results. The authors also examine reductions between OT protocols and extend the results to a generalized erasure channel. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize K-out-of-N oblivious transfer capacity over binary erasure channels, generalizing known 1-out-of-2 and 1-out-of-N results and analyzing reductions.

entry.title: TRIAGE-CPG: Testing How Language Models Sort Unknown Programs Into Benign, Suspicious, or Malicious Under Limited Analysis
entry.summary: TRIAGE-CPG: A Cross-Model Study of Budgeted Static Malware Triage with Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how large language models perform when security analysts use them to sort unknown Windows programs, given a fixed budget of code to inspect. The authors built TRIAGE-CPG, a fixed pipeline over a decompiled binary's code property graph, and tested eight models on 1,000 Windows PE binaries. The best model reached a strict balanced accuracy of 0.805 and a triage balanced accuracy of 0.855, after examining about 40 of roughly 1,000 functions per binary. The models followed different triage policies, and the authors conclude that no single configuration works best universally.

entry.title: Verifiable random sampling of private data without a single trusted party
entry.summary: Verifiable Random Sampling of Private Data Without a Trusted Single Party arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper addresses the problem that auditors cannot tell whether a disclosed sample of private data was drawn at random or cherry-picked to hide flaws. It proposes NoCherry, in which the data holder commits to hashes of all dataset items with independent servers, and the sample is chosen using a decentralized randomness beacon value emitted two rounds after the commitment. Servers return signed receipts so anyone can later verify the revealed sample matches the prescribed selection. The approach applies to audits such as private AI benchmarks, dataset quality claims, and security reviews.

entry.title: Chronos: Reproducing TOCTOU Races into Reusable Security Regression Tests
entry.summary: Taking Time Out of TOCTOU: From Race Reproduction to Security Discovery arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents Chronos, a framework that reproduces time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race vulnerabilities and builds reusable one-trial security regression oracles for deterministic reproduction, commit bisection, and CI. It uses seccomp notifications, ptrace, and a KVM guest gate to enforce declared timing between hold, attack, and release at syscall and instruction sites, and a single decision procedure labels runs as vulnerable, fixed, or indeterminate. On known-vulnerable builds, Chronos produced no false-fixed classifications, while effect-only checkers produced over 800 in failed-intervention trials. Applied to releases and packages, it helped uncover three issues, including incomplete fixes in chrony and rpm. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors separate intervention timing from verdict evidence and enforce attack ordering with seccomp; they report validation on 17 syscall cases, historical bisections, and finding several incomple

entry.title: Post-Quantum Crypto Migration: Performance Profiling of TLS Algorithms
entry.summary: PQC Migration: End-to-End Performance Profiling of Post Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms in mTLS arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper measures end-to-end performance of TLS 1.3 connections using NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid key exchange algorithms under various network conditions. It evaluates speed (throughput, connection time) and sustainability (energy, CPU cycles). The authors find that standardized post-quantum algorithms cause no measurable degradation, while hybrid algorithms show noticeable slowdowns that worsen under poor network conditions, so migration should be network-condition aware.

entry.title: Internet-facing exposure and fixes in France's maritime sector: a passive scan of 129 organisations
entry.summary: Exposure and remediation in the French maritime sector: a passive measurement of 129 organisations arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper passively measures the internet-facing attack surface of 129 maritime organisations, 103 French companies and 26 international operators active in French waters, using public DNS, email-authentication, TLS certificate and web data. After manual verification, 475 findings were retained, about 3.7 per organisation. 46% of organisations had at least one high or critical finding, and French companies fared worse than international operators. The authors sent individual reports to 43 domains in March 2026, rescanned 123 organisations in November 2026, and compared remediation rates between notified and non-notified organisations.

entry.title: AudioTrace: File-Level Membership Detection for Audio Language Models
entry.summary: AudioTrace: File-Level Membership Detection for Audio Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies whether a given audio recording was used to train an audio large language model, a question raised by privacy and copyright concerns. It introduces AudioTraceBench, a benchmark of 1,285 recordings with fine-tuning membership labels, and shows that existing text- and video-based methods perform near random guessing on audio. The proposed AudioTrace method generates audio-conditioned proxy questions with the target model and aggregates membership evidence per recording, reaching an AUROC of 0.60 and outperforming existing baselines.

entry.title: Risk certificates for finding multiple vulnerabilities in parametric Markov decision process models
entry.summary: Scenario-Based Risk Certificates for Multi-Property Vulnerability Discovery in Parametric MDPs arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies how to find parameter settings that break several safety or performance requirements at once in parametric Markov decision processes (pMDPs), where transition probabilities depend on uncertain parameters. It builds candidate vulnerability regions for each requirement and analyzes random testing budgets under a given parameter distribution. The method has two layers: a scenario-approximation layer giving PAC guarantees for conservative vulnerability regions, and a testing layer that yields a stopping certificate computed from region masses alone. A composition theorem bounds the expected non-discovery score.00

entry.title: ProcReverser: Automated Black-Box Reverse Engineering of Processor Microarchitecture for Vulnerability Analysis
entry.summary: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering when processor implementation details are unavailable. It uses execution feedback to refine experiment plans and test programs, and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. The system targets hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, including speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. It was evaluated on the XuanTie C910, gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and SiFive P550.

entry.title: Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: a public catalog of network-traffic datasets for AI security research
entry.summary: The Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which Data for AI in Cybersecurity? arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents a public, continuously updated catalog of cybersecurity datasets based on network traffic, linking to original sources rather than hosting data. The first release reviews 234 datasets across 14 domains using a seven-axis taxonomy. The authors note that the field grows quickly but unevenly, and they discuss dataset selection and benchmark pitfalls for AI research.

entry.title: STA: A split temporal attack method for testing how well multimodal RL driving policies withstand timing errors
entry.summary: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper argues that multimodal reinforcement learning driving policies depend on sensor observations being temporally aligned, so timing inconsistencies can cause decision failures. The authors propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under budget and policy-aware constraints, delaying observations using historical states. In CARLA experiments, STA more than doubles the collision rate of the strongest baseline against a PPO policy while using 17.8% fewer attack attempts, and it also generalizes to a VLM-based driving policy.

entry.title: A first study of System One decision models for malware detection
entry.summary: A First Look at System One Decision Models for Malware Detection arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents the first evaluation of System One decision models for detecting malware in Windows Portable Executable files. The authors decompile binaries with Ghidra and capa, render the results as a textual state, and propose S1Mal, an ensemble combining typed answers and the CLM-8B embedding. Experiments on BODMAS, SOREL-20M and benign files show higher detection at a fixed false positive rate, with decisions backed by readable atomic answers.

entry.title: MASTA: A multi-agent system that turns protocol descriptions into Tamarin security models
entry.summary: MASTA: A Feedback-Scheduled Multi-Agent System for End-to-End Tamarin Modeling and Analysis arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents MASTA, a multi-agent system that converts natural-language security protocol descriptions into complete formal models for Tamarin verification. It divides work among an Architect for rule modeling, an Auditor for property modeling, and an Arbiter that schedules the next agent based on verifier feedback and a six-class problem taxonomy. On a benchmark of 10 protocols with 139 mutation variants, MASTA outperforms OpenCode on the same backbone and ranks first on correctness and completeness averages.

entry.title: Experience report: ENTRAP, an IaC enterprise cyber range for reproducible security assessment and dataset generation
entry.summary: Experience: ENTRAP - An IaC Enterprise Cyber Range for Reproducible Security Assessment and Dataset Generation arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents ENTRAP, an Infrastructure-as-Code cyber range that defines a fully segmented enterprise network as version-controlled automation using Ansible, KVM/Libvirt, and Cloud-init, and can reset it to a clean state. Three attacks are run on the network: a ransomware campaign backed by Ransomware-as-a-Service, DHCP starvation with rogue DHCP, and perimeter web exploitation, producing labeled attack datasets. The authors train a Random Forest classifier for ransomware detection on this data and report its evaluation. The codebase, logs, and datasets are publicly released.

entry.title: Governing AI-Recommended Security Changes with a State Machine: A Paired-Scenario Study
entry.summary: State-Machine Governance of Adaptive Enforcement: Evidence from a Paired-Scenario Evaluation arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper examines how to govern the execution of rapid policy changes recommended by AI-assisted security systems, using explicit authorization, evidence, and recovery rules. The authors implemented a machine-verifiable, state-machine-governed transition procedure in ZTGuard and tested it on 36 matched scripted scenarios with deterministic vendor-connector simulations. The governed procedure scored a mean Control of 0.972, compared with 0.720 for the scripted operator-driven baseline, a difference that was statistically significant (p < .001). The authors state that the findings support controlled artifact utility rather than production readiness.

entry.title: ReconPotBench: A Multi-Round Benchmark for Testing AI Honeypots in Linux Reconnaissance
entry.summary: ReconPotBench: Evaluating LLM Honeypots in Multi-Round Linux Reconnaissance arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper introduces ReconPotBench, a benchmark for evaluating honeypots that imitate Linux systems and use large language models, across multi-round reconnaissance interactions. It includes 1,032 three-round interactions with reference outputs from a real Linux environment. The study compares Cowrie with open-source and closed-source language models on authenticity, consistency across rounds, and reconnaissance value. Results show that LLM honeypots are more authentic and useful than Cowrie but less consistent, and that authenticity declines as interactions deepen.

entry.title: Reconstructing an incomplete patch bypass in LLM agent frameworks
entry.summary: Beyond the Patch: Reconstructing an Incomplete-Fix Patch Bypass in LLM Agent Frameworks with Control-Gated, Benign Probes arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents a benign, control-gated method for reconstructing vulnerabilities and reports a pilot study across four LLM agent frameworks. For PraisonAI 4.6.31, the original tool-loading trigger is blocked, but a sibling tool_override path still violates the security invariant, reproducing the publicly documented CVE-2026-44334 bypass of CVE-2026-40287. For CrewAI, a violation appears in release 1.11.0 and confinement in 1.11.1.

entry.title: Replay-Augmented Regularisation for Class-Incremental Network Intrusion Detection: EWC and LwF Evaluated on Three Datasets
entry.summary: Replay-Augmented Regularisation for Class-Incremental Network Intrusion Detection: A Three-Dataset Evaluation of EWC and LwF arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in network intrusion detection models that are updated sequentially as new attack categories appear. A one-dimensional CNN is trained over nine sequential tasks on UNSW-NB15, ToN-IoT and CIC-IDS2017, comparing plain fine-tuning with Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) and Learning without Forgetting (LwF). EWC and LwF are evaluated with and without a rehearsal buffer of 20% of previous classes. Replay substantially improves final accuracy, though the authors do not claim that the regularisers add benefit beyond replay alone.

entry.title: Unified watermarking and tiered access control for text-to-image diffusion models via a single prompt
entry.summary: Beyond Semantic Prompts: Unified Watermarking and Access Control for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper proposes a unified framework that embeds customizable multi-bit watermarks into text-to-image diffusion outputs and enforces tiered access using a single text prompt. Training has two stages: first, watermark messages are represented as designated words with learnable protocol-token embeddings, guided by a frozen reference model and a pretrained watermark codec; second, a prompt-structure recognition network modulates the VAE decoder to output clear watermarked images, blurred previews, or black outputs depending on access state. Experiments report reliable watermark recovery and robustness to common image-processing operations and model modifications.

entry.title: Building AI test models that deliberately hide deception to stress-test audits
entry.summary: Designing Deceptive Model Organisms that Successfully Evade Auditing arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies deceptive AI behaviors such as sandbagging, where a model intentionally underperforms on evaluations. The authors design three deceptive model organisms, two optimized against blackbox auditing and one against both blackbox and whitebox auditing. They argue these models satisfy requirements of effectiveness, utility preservation, and robustness to auditing, providing worst-case baselines for evaluating future auditing techniques.

entry.title: KVMark: A Fragile Watermark for Checking KV-Cache Integrity Between AI Agents
entry.summary: KVMARK: Fragile Watermarking for KV-Cache Integrity in Latent Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper addresses latent multi-agent systems, where transformer agents pass key-value cache tensors directly to each other instead of text, a channel vulnerable to man-in-the-middle tampering. It proposes KVMark, a training-free, zero-bit watermarking framework that verifies handoff integrity using position-dependent sign patterns, per-head detection, depth-aware strength scheduling, and content-bound key derivation. On a four-agent latent pipeline, the authors report 100% detection across 1,500 handoffs with 0.0% false positives and 17/17 attacked layers localized, with no significant reasoning accuracy loss.

entry.title: Field-sensitive taint analysis for C using interval-based heap tracking
entry.summary: Taint Analysis via Heap-Aware Propagation arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper presents a field-sensitive taint analysis for C that combines Data Structure Analysis with data-flow tracking of explicit dependencies. It identifies a precision loss in existing DSA-style analyses for structs mixing scalar fields with a flexible array member accessed by symbolic indices. The authors propose I-DSA, which represents field positions as intervals. Experiments report fewer false alarms at little pointer-analysis cost and better scalability than PhASAR on real-world programs.

entry.title: Where the Evidence Lives: Privacy and Diagnosability of AI-Agent Trace Exports
entry.summary: Where the Evidence Lives: Measuring Privacy and Diagnosability of Exported AI-Agent Traces arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies how to export AI-agent execution traces so they can still diagnose failures without exposing customer identities. The authors built an executable benchmark on synthetic multi-tenant workflows that measures what an export reveals and whether a proposed repair restores correct output. Two export methods, comparison facts and execution-scoped pseudonyms, kept repairs working while the tested identifier matchers identified no requested customer. However, row counts still exposed identities, and removing selected counters stopped that attack.

entry.title: Where the Saved Time Goes: Limits of Hiding Cross-Tenant Cache Hits in LLM Serving
entry.summary: Where the Savings Go: The Limits of Hiding Cross-Tenant Cache Hits in LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 16, 2026LLM serving engines cache prompt prefixes, so a shared cache can reveal whether other tenants have sent a given text through faster responses. The paper shows that common defenses that hide cache hits fall short, because the saved time is passed to requests queued behind the hit and can be detected by an attacker within normal rate limits. On one vLLM instance, a single probe detects cached texts of 256 tokens or more with advantage at least 0.98. The authors also prove that a tenant's gain from other accounts' content is bounded by the allowed leakage, so at zero leakage only the provider keeps the savings. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show hit-hiding defenses overlook where saved time goes, prove tenant gain bounds leakage, and report a single probe detecting cached prompts on vLLM.

entry.title: A bit-by-bit oracle attack on RSA padding using partial message knowledge
entry.summary: A Bleichenbacher bit-by-bit oracle attack from partial message knowledge arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper shows how an attacker who knows a few least significant bytes of an RSA message can use a server's oracle side channel to recover the full message one bit at a time. It considers two oracles testable with chosen ciphertexts: one revealing whether the decrypted message starts with 00 02, and one revealing whether it is fully PKCS-compliant. The same method is also adapted to extract the few least significant bytes of the message, at higher cost.

entry.title: Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns About Healthcare AI
entry.summary: Understanding Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns in Healthcare AI Systems arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper analyzes 6,514 posts from 14 medical communities on Reddit to study how users discuss security, privacy, and trust concerns about healthcare AI and how these discussions change over time. Users see healthcare AI as expanding trust boundaries and attack surfaces through integrations with electronic health records, third-party services, cloud platforms, and automated clinical workflows. The authors identify four attitudes toward these risks: exploring accountability and harm, cautiously accepting AI with stronger safeguards, skepticism about trustworthiness, and resignation to data exposure and automation. Discussion volume has risen significantly, with shifts coinciding with major deployments, privacy incidents, and regulatory developments.

entry.title: Secure wearable sensors for monitoring soldier health: lessons from the CAPSARII project
entry.summary: Cyber-Secure Wearable, Ultra-Low-Power Networked Sensors for Soldier Health Monitoring: Insights from the CAPSARII project arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper presents the CAPSARII project, which develops a cyber-secure wearable platform and a battlefield Internet of Things framework for real-time monitoring of military personnel. Stress classification is benchmarked on a public wearable dataset, where XGBoost reaches about 0.901 accuracy and a feature-based Transformer achieves the highest AUC of 0.963. The authors also outline remaining challenges, including signal-quality validation, low-latency communication, and post-quantum cryptography on constrained devices.

entry.title: HEAMS: A Holistic Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Memory Systems
entry.summary: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper argues that AI agent memory systems, which store users' information across interactions, should be judged on responsibilities beyond task performance and efficiency, including security, privacy, and user sovereignty. The authors present HEAMS, an open-source framework that states these desiderata, assembles a benchmark suite covering them, and includes a prototype memory system, MilaMem, plus a governance layer that can wrap any memory system. Comparing memory systems, they find that no system leads every performance benchmark and that strong performance can coexist with weak privacy and security scores. They also report that governance policies strongly affect results.

entry.title: Sequential Semantic and Non-Semantic Watermarking: Testing Resistance to UnMarker Removal Attacks
entry.summary: Sequential Semantic-Non-Semantic Watermarking: Robustness Against UnMarker Attacks arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies Sequential Semantic Non-Semantic Watermarking (SSNSW), which combines the HiDDeN and StegaStamp watermarking methods. Using 50 images from MS-COCO and CelebA-HQ, the authors test both embedding orders and apply UnMarker's non-semantic and semantic removal attacks individually and in sequence. Both watermarks stay largely decodable after dual embedding, and single attacks usually leave one watermark strong, so sequential attacks are needed to reduce both. Low LPIPS scores in several settings coexist with visible distortions in some facial images, so LPIPS alone is not a sufficient quality measure.

entry.title: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda-Seeding Attacks
entry.summary: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda Seeding against Research Planning arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper systematizes security research on deep research and agentic search agents across four stages: retrieval, planning, evidence integration, and report generation. It presents a unified threat model, a taxonomy of attacks and defenses, and a review of evaluation benchmarks. The authors propose an agenda seeding attack that introduces a fictitious evaluation metric without any instructions, and report that across 3,520 sandboxed runs it made the target the top pick in 16% to 28% of reports. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose agenda seeding, which introduces a fictitious metric without instructions, and report it ranks the target first in 16% to 28% of 3,520 sandboxed runs.

entry.title: CHERI Under Fault Injection: Testing Whether Hardware Memory Safety Holds Up to Faults
entry.summary: CHERI under Fault Injection: An Emulation-Based Security Evaluation of Capability Hardware Enhanced RISC Instructions arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This thesis examines whether targeted fault injection can defeat the memory-safety guarantees of CHERI, a hardware architecture using capability pointers, in a pure-capability CHERI-RISC-V environment. The author implements fault injection in a QEMU-based emulator and demonstrates four attack scenarios: buffer overflows, control-flow hijacking, data-only attacks, and use-after-free. The results show that a single or small number of targeted faults can succeed, indicating CHERI's guarantees depend on metadata integrity, uninterrupted checks, and revocation bitmap integrity. The thesis proposes mitigations including ECC-protected capability memory, field authentication codes, redundant checks, and revocation bitmap verification.

entry.title: Overly Aggressive Recovery: Understanding and Fixing Risky Fallbacks in LLM Agents
entry.summary: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper studies risky fallback, where an LLM agent switches to a substitute tool after an ordinary failure and crosses an action boundary, such as a forced push that deletes another author's commits. An empirical study of 304 scenarios across eight domains and 55 real CVEs found that all four evaluated models exhibit it, with action-boundary violations in up to 96.8% of risky scenarios. The authors propose nrepair, which scores the agent's context before each substitute tool call with a monitor calibrated on normal runs and withholds the call once when triggered. It cuts violations by up to 76.0% across the four models and is similarly effective on Claude Code and Codex.

entry.title: HalluProbe: Using VLM Hallucinations to Detect Backdoors
entry.summary: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection arXiv · Nov 15, 2026Vision-Language Models can be compromised by backdoors planted through poisoned training data. The paper finds that backdoored models hallucinate the backdoor target token more often across diverse inputs, while clean models' hallucinated tokens are random. Based on this, the authors propose HalluProbe, which amplifies hallucinations during decoding and measures how consistent the hallucinated tokens are to identify backdoored models. Tested against six backdoor attacks on three models, it reportedly achieves over 90% accuracy and outperforms existing detection methods.

entry.title: Local order matters: a lightweight CPU-trainable CNN for website fingerprinting on defended Tor traffic
entry.summary: Local Order Matters: A Lightweight CPU-Trainable CNN for Website Fingerprinting on Defended Tor Traffic arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies website fingerprinting attacks that infer which site a Tor user visits from encrypted cell sequences. The authors propose a compact 95,103-parameter 1-D convolutional network, trained on CPU, that processes the raw cell-direction sequence. Against the FRONT padding defense on a 95-site closed-world dataset, it reaches 54.2% top-1 accuracy, above the strongest feature baseline at 38.5%. A controlled experiment that permutes traffic cell order drops accuracy to 7.6%, showing the model relies heavily on order information.

entry.title: Where rank-1 difference-in-means refusal intervention works in multimodal model derivatives
entry.summary: Where Is Rank-1 DiM Refusal Intervenable in Multimodal LM Derivatives? arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies where safety refusal behavior can be intervened on in open-weight multimodal language model derivatives, using a shared mean and rank-1 difference-in-means protocol. It compares intervening at the text decoder against the vision encoder, projector, and fusion components. On mixed-input tests, text-side intervention raised attack success rates while the same intervention at the other components did not. The authors frame this as a result specific to their recipe, not as evidence that refusal is absent outside the text decoder.]

entry.title: Backdoors that can be switched off: attacks on robot vision-language-action models
entry.summary: When Backdoors Can Be Switched Off: Suppression-Aware Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies a type of backdoor attack on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot models, where several triggers must be present together to activate it and a natural-language instruction can suppress the malicious behavior. The authors design three variants: Cross-Modal Trigger, Self-Suppressing Trigger, and Multi-Trigger. They test these attacks with SmolVLA and OpenVLA models. The attacks reportedly evade detection methods such as Isolation Forest and STRIP while keeping clean-task performance intact.

entry.title: Attacks That Chain Harmless Tools in Autonomous Coding Agents, and a Defense Against Them
entry.summary: Compositional Exploits in Autonomous Coding Agents: Attack Mechanics and Ephemeral Defense arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper argues that auditing each tool in isolation is fundamentally insufficient for autonomous coding agents. It introduces compositional exploits, in which an agent chains individually harmless tool operations across turns using shared workspace files, environment variables, and chat memory to carry out an unauthorized attack. The authors also present CompGuard, a defense combining a cognitive control plane with an operating-system kernel enforcement layer to block such chains.

entry.title: Found but Not Fixed: Iterative LLM Pipelines from Vulnerability Discovery to Code Repair
entry.summary: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper notes that software vulnerability detection has improved, but manual code repair remains slow, costly, and can introduce new issues. The authors propose a generalized framework using large language models in a multi-stage feedback loop to automatically repair vulnerable functions in real-world code. They benchmark it against GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash and report that the pipeline can achieve high-quality repairs. The evaluation framework, fine-tuned weights, and experimental dataset are released on the authors' website.

entry.title: Reduced Attack Diversity in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
entry.summary: Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper examines how reinforcement-learning-trained automated red-teaming attackers can become more successful while producing a narrower range of attacks. The experiment uses a Qwen2.5-14B attacker and a DPO-trained Phi-4-mini defender, evaluated on 26 AdvBench behaviors across three runs. After 12 rounds, the Attack Diversity Retention scores were 0.63, 0.61 and 0.63, below the 0.75 threshold, while attack success continued to improve.

entry.title: Multi-agent authorization that protects systems but leaves users stranded
entry.summary: Protecting the System, Stranding the User: The Limits of Multi-Agent Authorization arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper argues that current multi-agent authorization architectures prioritize system integrity and shift the cost of failure onto human operators. It analyzes four structural weaknesses: the unverifiable nature of user intent, dynamic trust scores that fail across multi-agent handoffs, safely halted workflows that strand users, and a possible moral hazard from frictionless automated recovery. The authors propose an architectural synthesis linking deterministic security to human outcomes and discuss unresolved theoretical limits.

entry.title: ElevatorII: A Fast, Fully Static Translator for Running x86 Programs on AArch64
entry.summary: ElevatorII: High-Performance Fully-Static Cross-ISA Binary Translation arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper presents ElevatorII, a fully static, ahead-of-time binary-to-binary compiler that translates x86 programs to AArch64 without requiring run-time support on the target. It combines superset disassembly, which pre-translates every possible byte interpretation, with observation-guided path selection to create optimized code paths. On 11 SPEC CPU 2026 Integer benchmarks without C++ exceptions, it runs at about 2.5 times native AArch64 time, while output code is about 51 times the size of source-compiled code, with only 2-3% of code being hot.

entry.title: TrustBound: Machine-Checked Completeness for Payment Epochs Started by AI Agents
entry.summary: TrustBound: Mechanized Completeness for Payment Epochs Initiated by AI Agents arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies when a trusted payment service can account for every payment in an epoch and block later payments made under earlier authority. The authors build a Lean model in which operations are recorded before receiving execution authority, with both actions serialized by an admission fence. They prove that the fence fixes a journal covering all modeled effects and outstanding rights, that discharging those rights prevents further effects, and that truthful outcomes yield exact accounting. Concurrent experiments on an executable service also revealed a conflict from reordered provider reads, which serializing retrieval with journal updates removes.

entry.title: Agent Authenticator: A hardware-bound login design giving AI agents passkey-level security
entry.summary: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper addresses how AI coding agents authenticate to services such as code repositories, package registries and cloud APIs. Today they use long-lived tokens and API keys that can be stolen through prompt injection or malware on the same machine. The authors propose the Agent Authenticator, which gives agents passkey-like properties: per-service hardware-bound keys, origin binding enforced by the runtime, human-signed scoped mandates, and cross-device approval for high-risk actions. It is built as a profile over existing standards and also produces a signed, hash-chained record of each authorized action.

entry.title: VAST: Turning Real Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable Multi-Step Test Environments for LLM Red-Team Agents
entry.summary: VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents arXiv · Nov 15, 2026VAST (Verifiable Adversarial Scenario Training & Evaluation) is a declarative range compiler that separates vulnerability scenarios from an added workflow-hardening layer. On a TopicServer subset, supplying the full workflow protocol raised completion from 12/90 to 76/90 across three models. On a separate ranges_v2 ledger, a Redis worker-chaining intervention lifted solves from 0/18 to 18/18. The paper also compares three LoRA fine-tuning recipes on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct.

entry.title: Security Authentication as Protective Friction in e-Government Platforms
entry.summary: Security Authentication as Protective Friction: Understanding the Dual Effects of Authentication Measures in e-Government Platform arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines security authentication measures, such as facial recognition and multi-factor verification, on e-government platforms like government credit platforms. The authors reconceptualize these measures as protective friction and propose a dual-pathway model in which it reduces privacy-security risk perception while increasing effort cost, with self-efficacy moderating only the risk pathway. The research-in-progress outlines a mixed-methods design combining a user survey and staff interviews at a Chinese municipal credit center to test the model.

entry.title: Memorization in Diffusion Models Traced to a Few Attention Heads, with a Projection-Based Fix
entry.summary: Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies how diffusion models memorize and reproduce training samples during inference. The authors find that memorization is mainly driven by a small set of shallow-layer cross-attention heads rather than the whole mechanism.
