They propose Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression, which uses a semantic-control score to pick the most relevant heads and removes their condition-specific components via directional projection. Experiments across diffusion models and datasets show reduced memorization with better image quality than existing methods.

entry.title: Orbit AI: Testing AI Agents That Use Tools to Answer Workplace Questions
entry.summary: Orbit AI: Evaluating Tool-Augmented Agents For Enterprise Question Answering arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents Orbit AI, a tool-based retrieval-augmented generation system that uses a ReAct agent built with LangGraph to pull and combine information from three workspace sources. It compares a standalone LLM, document-only retrieval, and a multi-tool agent with access to all three sources. On 80 held-out questions, the full agent reached 86.25% accuracy, versus 60.00% for document-only RAG and 23.13% for the plain LLM.

entry.title: Theoretical limits of watermarking AI text with fixed or tunable shared randomness
entry.summary: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes a unified theory of statistical watermarking for large language models, framing detection as an independence test between generated text and common randomness, with embedder and detector designed jointly. It characterizes the fundamental performance limits under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. The authors find that optimizing the common randomness does not raise the best achievable performance, but it allows a fixed, deterministic, model-agnostic detector to reach optimal performance. They also quantify the performance gap for a practical setting using fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector. ★★★★ Notable: The authors cast LLM watermarking as an independence test with common randomness, characterizing fundamental detection limits under fixed and optimizable randomness and the performance gap for fixed u

entry.title: Optional Traps: How LLM Agents Respond to Fake Credentials and Alert-Driven Revocation
entry.summary: Optional Traps: An Empirical Study of LLM Agents Against Credential Deception and Alert-Driven Revocation arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper tests whether deception tools such as honeypots, decoys and canary credentials still work when the attacker is a large language model (LLM) agent. In an isolated lab, four studies found that after leaks are closed, deception added no measurable prevention beyond hardening but enabled fast, attributable detection and per-client revocation. All results are lab-scale and are not a production claim.

entry.title: Frozen safety-filter probes lose their calibrated operating point after model updates
entry.summary: Operating-Point Failure of Frozen Guardrail Probes Under Backbone Updates arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The authors froze a guardrail probe and its threshold and tracked its operating point across 18 test cells covering 16 public language-model updates. At a 1% target, the threshold failed in most cells, with the largest rise in false-positive rate going from 1.01% to 15.12%. The area under the ROC curve changed by at most 0.0058, so ranking performance stayed nearly constant while the operating point shifted.

entry.title: Injection attacks that make LLMs falsify industrial compliance documents
entry.summary: When the Spec Sheet Lies: Injection Attacks on LLM-Generated Compliance Artifacts arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines how prompt injection attacks can compromise large language models tasked with generating industrial documents such as Safety Data Sheets, Quality Control documents, and Digital Product Passports. The study finds that attack success varies significantly across models. Active falsification injections succeed most often across all scenarios, while models are most robust against passively injected override requests.

entry.title: Agent-ZTA: A Chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Runtime Security-State Propagation and Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation
entry.summary: Agent-ZTA: A chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Bidirectional Security-State Propagation and Runtime Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes Agent-ZTA, a Zero Trust authorization and containment model for multi-agent systems in which tasks and permissions are delegated along chains of autonomous agents. It separates each agent's path-specific delegated authority from the permissions currently usable under trusted policy, and defines bidirectional propagation so downstream security events can affect related upstream workflow states. The model specifies adaptive, branch-scoped containment using restricted permissions and an optional sandbox mode, and presents a deterministic decision procedure, five security properties, and worked authorization traces. The paper also states its trust assumptions and the exact scope of its security properties.

entry.title: Learned eavesdropping detection in BB84 quantum key distribution does not converge
entry.summary: No Convergence in Learned Eavesdropping-Detection Dynamics for BB84 Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies a game between a reinforcement-learning eavesdropper and a threshold-adapting detector in BB84 quantum key distribution. Using alternating best-response training across three learning rules and three channel-noise levels, the authors find that detection performance keeps fluctuating and does not settle to a fixed point. They conclude that a learned detector cannot be certified from any single round, and that closing the stealth window may require changing the information structure rather than out-adapting the attacker. Correction Nov 17, 2026: Moved from "Quantum Computing" to "Cryptography & Security"

entry.title: Reanalysis of quantum machine learning intrusion detection: false alarms and detection trade-offs
entry.summary: Reconstructing False Alarm and Detection Rates in Quantum Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper performs a secondary analysis of 25 records selected by Kaissar and colleagues, reconstructing false-positive rates, attack true-positive rates, and evaluation provenance in quantum machine learning intrusion detection studies. In one comparison, a quantum support vector machine lowers the false-positive rate from 6.875% to 3.329%, while the true-positive rate falls slightly from 93.955% to 93.682%. The authors stress that these findings are a reproducible interpretation rather than operational guarantees.

entry.title: AI Security Literacy: An Ecosystem-Based Competency Framework and K-12 Learning Platform
entry.summary: AI Security Literacy: Ecosystem-Based Competency Framework and K-12 Learning Platform arXiv · Oct 21, 2026This paper proposes an AI Security Literacy (AISL) framework with six dimensions covering the school ecosystem. Its technical dimensions draw on public AI-safety benchmarks and a reproducible multi-seed adversarial evaluation, while its attitudinal dimensions use nationally representative survey data from U.S. teachers and adults. The authors report that only 34.5% of teachers say their school has an AI policy. They also present NeuralFortify, a browser-based K-12 platform built on real AI models, as an illustrative implementation.

entry.title: Certifying Fraud-Rule Portfolios Against Synthetic Distribution Shift
entry.summary: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to choose fraud-detection rule portfolios that meet a precision or recall floor without overfitting the selection data. It compares point-estimate selection, a fixed safety margin, and one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bounds with Bonferroni adjustment. Across 6,400 datasets from two synthetic generators, full-validation certification reduced held-out floor violations by 29.1 percentage points on average versus point selection. The results vary by condition and do not estimate performance on real transaction populations.

entry.title: Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: checking the RFC 6979 security assumption and real implementations
entry.summary: Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: the RFC 6979 assumption, a counterexample, and the state of deployed implementations arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines the security assumption behind RFC 6979, which derives ECDSA signing nonces deterministically, and isolates it as an assumption called A*. It shows A* is separate from the PRF security of HMAC and from auxiliary-input PRF security, and gives a counterexample. An audit of 31 secp256k1 implementations finds that 28 sign deterministically without added entropy, and a deviation from libsecp256k1 before version 0.2.0 persists in several libraries. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors isolate assumption A* underlying RFC 6979, separate it from AI-PRF with counterexamples, and report an audit of 31 secp256k1 implementations.

entry.title: CANTraj: Rebuilding Vehicle Routes from CAN Signals in Real Driving
entry.summary: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper releases CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN vehicle signals with time-aligned GNSS trajectories, plus CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery. It shows that removing GPS coordinates does not remove location information, since signals such as speed and steering can be matched to road networks to recover routes. The authors report that with a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87% for an online map filter. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine steering signals with road-network constraints to recover trajectories from CAN data, comparing six attacks on a unified benchmark of 776 unseen drives.

entry.title: Classification of quadratic APN functions on F_2^10 with a prime-order self-equivalence
entry.summary: Quadratic APN Functions of 𝔽₂¹⁰ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper classifies quadratic APN functions on F_2^10 that have a linear self-equivalence of prime order, a property shared by all known APN permutations in even dimension. Of 299 possible types, 298 are settled, yielding 29 equivalence classes up to extended affine equivalence, four of them new. The one open type corresponds to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes, and the authors conjecture no further classes exist. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors classify quadratic APN functions over F_2^10 with prime-order linear self-equivalences, excluding 280 types and reporting four new classes.

entry.title: On the Same Track: Privacy Leaks in Electric Rail Transport via Magnetic Fields — how phone magnetometers can reveal train travel
entry.summary: On the Same Track: Privacy Leaks in Electric Rail Transport via Magnetic Fields arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper shows that electric trains generate distinctive magnetic fields that a smartphone magnetometer can capture, and that apps can read these signals without user permission. It presents two attacks on passenger privacy: determining whether a user is riding an electric train, and inferring whether other people are aboard the same train. Empirical tests across 217 train rides confirm both attacks are effective. The authors discuss countermeasures and argue that mobile operating systems should require explicit user permission to access the magnetometer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show electric train magnetic fields are capturable by phone magnetometers, enabling transport mode detection and colocation prediction, evaluated over 217 train rides with countermeasures

entry.title: Forget the Lineage: Forward-Secure Erasure for LLM-Agent Memory
entry.summary: Forget the Lineage: Forward-Secure, Lineage-Complete Cryptographic Erasure for LLM-Agent Memory arXiv · Nov 13, 2026LLM agents store long-term memories they write themselves, such as summaries and extracted facts, so deleting a message leaves derived copies behind. The paper introduces LinEra, which encrypts each memory with a key derived from its parents' keys along the derivation graph, so forgetting one source makes all its descendants unreadable. Experiments with real LLMs writing LoCoMo conversation memories show that an attacker with all storage and current keys recovers no forgotten secrets under LinEra. The trade-off is a larger forgetting radius, which grows with the writer's fan-in. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce lineage-complete forward-secure erasure via puncturable PRFs and derivation-graph keys, with proofs and LoCoMo experiments integrated with mem0.

entry.title: "Hello Again": Brute-forcing Windows Hello PINs by abusing replay-protected monotonic counters
entry.summary: Hello Again: Exploiting Replay Protected Monotonic Counters to Brute-Force Windows Hello PINs arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper analyzes RPMC (Replay Protected Monotonic Counters), a JEDEC-standard mechanism that protects firmware TPM state from rollback on x86 systems. The authors found that Winbond SPI flash leaks its HMAC key under voltage glitching, and AMD's NV controller does not verify RPMC increments. Together these flaws allow rollback of the fTPM's lockout counters. The authors report recovering a 4-digit Windows Hello PIN in 40 hours on locked, encrypted hardware, and say the same method weakens BitLocker's TPM+PIN protector. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first practical RPMC analysis on shipping x86 systems, finding Winbond key leakage and unchecked AMD increments enabling fTPM lockout rollback affecting Windows Hello and BitLo

entry.title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64 Code
entry.summary: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64 arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents DeCompCert, a decompiler verified in Rocq that reconstructs CompCert C code from AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It uses nine reverse passes that combine deductively verified transformations with translation validation, where untrusted analyses propose candidates and verified validators accept only those meeting the required semantic correspondence. The paper evaluates DeCompCert on about 2.16 million lines of C code. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine verified transformations with translation validation, give an end-to-end correctness theorem, and report validation rates over about 2.16 million lines of C.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving clustering and parameter selection for collaborative population stratification using distributed PCA
entry.summary: Privacy-Preserving Clustering Algorithm and Parameter Selection for Collaborative Population Stratification Using Distributed PCA arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes a privacy-preserving selection layer that lets an honest-but-curious server recommend a clustering method and hyperparameter setting from privacy-protected data. Parties share low-rank principal-component summaries through distributed PCA to build a common low-dimensional representation, then apply three local differential privacy pipelines (PCA then Noise, Noise then PCA, and Noise-Only). Experiments on openSNP and 1000 Genomes show the PCA-based pipelines outperform Noise-Only in clustering utility, communication cost, and runtime, and show lower membership-inference attack power at small privacy budgets.

entry.title: Memory Safety Is Not Enough: Code Reuse Attacks in Memory-Safe Languages
entry.summary: Memory Safety Isn't All You Need: Code Reuse Attacks in Memory Safe Languages arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper shows that memory safety blocks classic code reuse attacks based on arbitrary memory corruption, yet code reuse still occurs in memory-safe languages. It proposes a language-agnostic framework that splits an attack into a weakness, which fetches a value from shared runtime state, and a gadget, which passes that value to a sensitive sink. The framework covers five known attack classes, and the authors also organize existing defenses and present a formal model language.

entry.title: Measuring Risk of Membership Inference in Shared Genomic Data
entry.summary: Quantifying Membership Inference Risks in Genomic Data Sharing: The Role of Attacker's Auxiliary Information arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines how an attacker can determine whether a person's genomic data was used in a study, a risk to privacy in genomic data sharing. It proposes a pre-release auditing framework based on principal component analysis that applies local differential privacy and estimates attack power at a 5% false-positive rate. Experiments on the openSNP and 1000 Genomes datasets find that separation between the researcher's data and public auxiliary data is the main factor in attack success. The framework lets researchers assess dataset-specific risk before publication.

entry.title: Lasso: Fast, Low-Energy AI-Generated Media Detection Using Intel QAT Hardware Compression
entry.summary: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper reverse engineers the Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) compression accelerator and finds that processing time varies with the data structure. It uses this property to build Lasso, a detector for AI-generated content that treats the accelerator as a measuring instrument. The authors report higher text detection accuracy than several baselines, detection in 0.74 microseconds, and over 99% less energy per document. Lasso also detects AI-generated video, code, and images.

entry.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards in the Agent2Agent Protocol
entry.summary: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines security risks in Agent Cards, the machine-readable metadata used by the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol to let orchestrators discover external agents. Because these cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields, they can influence agent selection before invocation. The authors define ten manipulation attack types and propose SECCARD, a layered validation framework. Results show it detects attacks across all ten classes while preserving benign cards, but effectiveness varies substantially with the LLM judge used.

entry.title: Stargate: Security Analysis and Mission-Aware Firewall for CubeSat Space Protocol
entry.summary: Stargate: Security Analysis and Mission-Aware Firewall for the CubeSat Space Protocol arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper systematically analyzes the security model and attack surface of the CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP), a communication protocol widely used in CubeSat missions, and identifies limitations in its trust assumptions and mission-context awareness. Based on these findings, the authors build a taxonomy of CSP attacks in four classes and introduce Stargate, a modular, mission-aware firewall that enforces CSP-specific policies. On a virtual testbed based on a real CubeSat mission and flight software, Stargate blocks all 11 representative attacks with a median round-trip latency increase of 1.42 ms.

entry.title: Quasipolynomial quantum algorithm for a vector dihedral coset problem with smooth modulus
entry.summary: A Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem with Smooth Modulus arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm that recovers a hidden vector s in Z_q^n from samples of the form (|0,x⟩+|1,x+s⟩)/√2, the vector dihedral coset problem. When the modulus q is B-smooth, the algorithm runs with n^{O(B^{1+o(1)} log q)} B^{O(B^{2+o(1)} log q)} samples and time, which is quasipolynomial when B is polylogarithmic and q is polynomial in n. The method reduces the modulus one prime factor at a time and uses an Ivanyos–Santha sieving procedure to clear non-linear phase terms. The authors state that the result does not yield a new attack on LWE in any regime.

entry.title: Personalized adaptive federated learning for canine heart enlargement keypoint prediction
entry.summary: Personalized and Adaptive Federated Learning for Canine Cardiomegaly Keypoint Prediction arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents PAFL, a structure-aware personalized and adaptive federated learning framework for estimating the vertebral heart score (VHS) and classifying cardiomegaly from canine thoracic X-rays. The method predicts anatomical keypoints and computes VHS from their geometry, improving interpretability. It separates shared feature representations from client-specific adaptation modules and aggregates client contributions by dataset size and model quality. The authors report improved predictive performance over isolated training and existing federated learning methods.

entry.title: Swarm Shepherd: Defending Multi-Agent Systems Against Hidden, Persistent Compromise
entry.summary: Swarm Shepherd: Securing Multi-Agent Ecosystems Against Persistent Latent Compromise arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper defines the "Agentic Sleeper," an attacker who behaves legitimately at first to gain routing trust, then activates later across memory, agent logic, and infrastructure. The authors propose Swarm Shepherd, a defense framework with an inference filter for early warning and a backward trace-back module that attributes the entry point. Experiments on LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen report warnings at least three sessions before visible degradation and 0.69 top-1 trace-back accuracy.

entry.title: Matching Ship AIS Tracks to Satellite RF Detections for Maritime Monitoring
entry.summary: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines how to link space-based radio frequency (RF) vessel detections with Automatic Identification System (AIS) trajectories to monitor maritime activity. The authors apply a Pair Hidden Markov Model that uses temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies, and evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections. Results show a top-1 precision of 0.7776 on multi-candidate detections, while a time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting performs better overall (precision 0.9013).

entry.title: VellSSLH: Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR Guided by Security Types
entry.summary: VellSSLH: Sound Type-Guided Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents VellSSLH, a method that selectively inserts speculative load hardening into LLVM IR to stop constant-time cryptographic programs from leaking secrets during speculative execution. Programmers annotate Public and Secret inputs, and an analysis infers which values may become secret, so protections are added only where needed. The authors prove in Rocq that programs accepted by their checker satisfy speculative constant-time security. On 24 cryptographic entries, VellSSLH shows 4.03% lower geometric-mean runtime than LLVM SLH.

entry.title: Adaptable Watermarking: Upgrading Image Watermark Models with Lightweight Adapters
entry.summary: Adaptable Watermarking: Transforming Image Watermarking Models via Lightweight Adapters arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper examines whether one neural image watermarking method can be converted into another through lightweight adaptation. The authors propose a framework that makes encoder-decoder watermarking models modular and upgradable, supporting multiple watermarking styles without full retraining. Adaptation attaches a compact parameter-efficient adapter and is fine-tuned with a multi-domain residual alignment loss and a secret-loss term that preserves bit accuracy. The approach is evaluated on several recent models, including TrustMark, InvisMark, RoSteALS, HiDDeN, and WAM.

entry.title: Information-theoretic threshold designated-verifier signatures for constrained devices
entry.summary: Information-Theoretic Threshold Designated-Verifier Digital Signatures for Resource-Constrained Devices arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper proposes three new information-theoretic threshold designated-verifier digital signature schemes: n-of-n multi-signature, t-of-n with a dealer, and t-of-n without a dealer. The authors prove security against any adversary under the standard security criterion. They evaluate signing and verification times on a Raspberry Pi 4 and compare performance with a comparable post-quantum threshold signature scheme.

entry.title: PrivacyPR: A Real-World Privacy Fix Dataset for Testing Privacy-Aware Code Review
entry.summary: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents PrivacyPR, a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests from 1,469 repositories, including 1,169 high-confidence privacy fixes and 1,643 non-fix PRs with commits, diffs, review discussions, and labels. An evaluation harness reverts each fix to reintroduce the defect, allowing benchmarking of coding agents. Two agents detected only 42-51% of defects under a generic review prompt, but 88-91% when explicitly asked to check privacy, while flagging 11-15% of non-fix PRs. The dataset and tools are publicly available.

entry.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Capturing Live GPU Hidden States for Request-Level Analysis
entry.summary: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents a method for extracting per-layer residual-stream activations from a running GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without needing prior knowledge of the model's architecture or weights. The authors validated the acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, finding the recovered bytes to be byte-exact. As an application, linear probes trained on standard framework activations were applied to the recovered states, distinguishing refusal from compliance with an AUROC of 0.88 on held-out prompts.

entry.title: Beyond Bot Labels: Ranking Shopping Sessions by the Cache Harm They Cause
entry.summary: Beyond Bot Labels: Retrospective Consequence-Grounded Ranking of Attributed Cache Harm in E-Commerce Logs arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies how automated traffic can evict objects that shoppers reuse, lowering the web cache hit ratio. Instead of detecting bots from User-Agent strings or behavior, it ranks sessions by the eviction damage they cause, attributed through a chronological replay of the logs. On a 12.7-million-request real trace, the top 1% of sessions account for 48.8% of attributed harm, and 49.1% of that top tier comes from sessions without bot tags.

entry.title: Condensing Law of Security Information: A Tradeoff Between Model Size and Retained Security Signals
entry.summary: Condensing Law of Security Information arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper argues that larger language models do not always perform better on security tasks, because they can silently repair anomalous inputs before a downstream security component sees them, erasing security-relevant signals. The authors formalize a tradeoff between a model's cognitive capability and the security information retained in its intermediate representations, using information-theoretic bounds. They conclude that usable security information is unimodal in model size, so security generalization error is U-shaped with an optimal finite model size. The authors call this the condensing law and report experiments on various real-world LLMs that they say validate it.

entry.title: Game-theoretic analysis of RIS-based challenge-response authentication, Part II: partial channel knowledge
entry.summary: Game-Theoretic Analysis of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response PLA - Part II: Partial Channel Knowledge arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies physical layer authentication in which a user Alice communicates with an authenticator Bob through a reconfigurable intelligent surface controlled by Bob, while an attacker Trudy tries to impersonate Alice. Part II assumes each agent observes only its own channel and models the attack-defense interaction as a finite-action Bayesian game, characterizing its Bayesian Nash equilibrium. Simulations in geometric and 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi-NLOS channels show that authentication performance depends on available spatial degrees of freedom, channel correlation, and operating signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed equilibrium strategies balance communication rate and security better than conventional benchmark policies.

entry.title: RuralShield: AI-Assisted Security Triage and Serverless Infrastructure for Resource-Limited Healthcare
entry.summary: RuralShield: Super Intelligence-Assisted Security Triage and Serverless Infrastructure for Resource-Constrained Healthcare arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents RuralShield, a system that links cloud security controls to an operational response process for healthcare providers with limited resources. Language-model assessments are checked in a structured way, routed deterministically, and turned into containment actions only after human approval. The design separates workload access, assessment validation, and action authorization so that each step produces inspectable records. The authors evaluate the implementation with a 120-hour non-AI workload and separate desktop and AWS AI test groups, reporting request success, latency, and restoration of settings after containment.

entry.title: Designing Multi-Agent Systems to Resist Malicious Agents
entry.summary: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design arXiv · Nov 13, 2026Multi-agent systems split complex tasks into subtasks, assign them to agents, and combine the agents' responses with an aggregation rule. The paper proposes response manipulation attacks (ReMA), which iteratively refine malicious responses to steer the final outcome. It also introduces SecMAS, an aggregation rule that selects the response most consistent with a large subset of other responses, and reports theoretical security guarantees and experiments showing it resists the evaluated attacks while keeping utility comparable to existing rules.

entry.title: Study showing LLMs can be fooled by malicious requests that look normal
entry.summary: LLMs are Vulnerable to Malicious Requests with Indistinguishable Intent arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies jailbreak attacks that bypass safety mechanisms in large language models. It finds that requests resembling normal user queries pass an LLM-based filter more often than those with obvious anomalous patterns. The authors introduce Detail Guidance Attack (DGA), which uses an auxiliary LLM to build detailed requests, and report high attack success rates across 11 victim models. The paper also evaluates a DGA-aware filter and includes a user study on everyday requests with ambiguous or dual-use intent.

entry.title: Survey of Post-Quantum Cryptography Integration in Software Development
entry.summary: SoK: Assessing Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption in Software Development: Standards, Lifecycle Coverage, Deployment Maturity, and Evidence of Readiness arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper systematises existing approaches to integrating post-quantum cryptography (PQC) into software development, covering implementation, migration, and developer education. The authors analyse these approaches against NIST PQC standards and migration guidance, along with lifecycle coverage and testing evidence. They find that prior work builds useful technical and organisational foundations but offers disconnected support across the software lifecycle, with evaluations concentrated in controlled or early-stage settings. The paper identifies cross-cutting gaps and calls for lifecycle-oriented, empirically validated approaches.

entry.title: Sum-checking SmallWood: smaller hash-based zero-knowledge proofs
entry.summary: Sum-Checking SmallWood: Smaller Hash-Based Zero-Knowledge Arguments IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents SmallWood+, an enhanced version of SmallWood that uses sum-check-based protocols to further reduce proof sizes. The authors formalize a Sum-Check Verification Constraint System (SVCS) and design generic compilers that turn these instances into zero-knowledge arguments. Applied to hash functions, proving 1 and 100 Keccak permutations requires 18 KB and 63 KB, compared with 29 KB and 127 KB for the best previous schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an SVCS framework and generic compilers, reporting smaller hash-based ZK proofs for Keccak permutations than prior schemes.

entry.title: RRHL: a relational logic for proving Rényi differential privacy in private learning
entry.summary: RRHL: A Relational Logic for Rényi Differential Privacy of Private Learning IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper introduces RRHL, a relational program logic for proving Rényi differential privacy of imperative programs that use continuous sampling. Its judgments give privacy budget bounds for instructions as functions of program states, and budget composition is sharp. The authors apply RRHL to several variants of DP-SGD and DP-FTRL and to gradient descent with per-record Rényi filters, matching the best known bounds in several cases. The logic, its soundness proof, and the case studies are formalized in Lean. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a relational logic for Rényi differential privacy, formalized in Lean, and report that case-study bounds match best known analyses.

entry.title: Limits of pseudorandom codes when the decoding key can be stolen
entry.summary: Limits of Pseudorandom Codes under Adaptive Corruption IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026Pseudorandom codes hide messages in strings that look uniformly random without the decoder key. The paper asks how many key bits are needed when the key may be stolen after some codewords have been sent. The authors introduce q-use codes and show that every adaptively secure pseudorandom code yields one with the same key length, so the lower bounds hold unconditionally. They prove that each opening costs extra key bits beyond the message length, with the cost depending on whether there is no noise, random noise, or error correction. They also show that a programmable random oracle cannot avoid this cost under noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce q-use codes and prove unconditional key-length lower bounds for adaptively secure PRCs, plus a robustness cost and random-oracle limits.

entry.title: Early-stopping broadcast for dishonest majorities with optimal rounds
entry.summary: Early-Stopping Dishonest Majority Broadcast with Optimal Round Complexity IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents a deterministic early-stopping broadcast protocol whose termination depends on the number f of actually corrupted parties rather than the worst-case bound t. Every honest party outputs and terminates within min{f+3, t+1} rounds. The protocol works in the dishonest-majority regime and achieves optimal round complexity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a deterministic early-stopping broadcast protocol achieving optimal $\min\{f+3,t+1\}$ rounds in the dishonest-majority regime, answering an open question.

entry.title: Byzantine Agreement with Signature Tokens: Using Quantum Cryptography to Exceed the One-Third Fault Limit
entry.summary: Byzantine Agreement with Signature Tokens IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies how quantum cryptography can help distributed consensus, focusing on Byzantine Agreement under partial synchrony, where each party holds k signature tokens. The authors design a protocol secure against a fraction of faults up to (2^(k+1)-1)/(2^(k+2)-1), and show that with k=Θ(log n) it solves the problem assuming only an honest majority. They also prove that Ω(log n) tokens are necessary, and that the 3/7 threshold achieved for k=1 is optimal. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show signature tokens let partial-synchrony Byzantine agreement exceed one-third faults, with an Ω(log n) lower bound and a tight 3/7 bound for k=1.

entry.title: Secure multiparty computation with minimal overhead and no circuit transformation
entry.summary: Multiparty Computation with Minimal Overhead without Circuit Transformation IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies secure multiparty computation, aiming to bring the total computation of all parties close to the cost of insecure circuit evaluation, an overhead of Õ(1). Earlier protocols over prime fields for general circuits required costly circuit transformations. The authors present an MPC protocol with Õ(1) overhead for any prime field, or integer ring Z_p, whose size needs only be n^{Ω(n)}, where n is the number of parties, instead of n^{Ω(n²)}. It requires no circuit transformation. The work extends the share unpacking technique of Garg et al. and develops a new approach to linear randomness extraction over integers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend share unpacking to prime fields of size n^Omega(n), avoiding circuit transformation while keeping near-constant overhead, plus a new integer linear randomness extraction tool.

entry.title: Batching and packing techniques for more efficient verifiable computation on CKKS encrypted data
entry.summary: Batch, Pack, and Prove: More Efficient Verifiable Computation for CKKS IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper addresses how to verify that computations on CKKS homomorphic encryption ciphertexts were performed correctly. It introduces a more efficient arithmetization, the BatchFold polynomial commitment for batched evaluations, a packing technique that removes the O(N) overhead in range proofs, and the SparsePack protocol for sparse polynomials. Evaluated on a generic neural network architecture, the approach yields proofs several orders of magnitude smaller and faster than prior work.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Analysis and Repair of Systemic Portfolio Risk
entry.summary: Privacy-Preserving Systemic Portfolio Analysis and Repair IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents a privacy-preserving framework that lets mutually distrustful financial institutions jointly identify systemic risk from overlapping portfolios and common liquidity shocks, and coordinate concrete portfolio adjustments without revealing their holdings. It uses secure multi-party computation (MPC) and also offers a federated variant that moves fund-local computation outside MPC while keeping global coordination secure. The authors implement the framework on real, publicly available portfolios, reporting private analysis in about 1 to 4 minutes and repair in 2.6 to 8.8 hours under MPC or 13 to 21 minutes in the federated setting.

entry.title: A Note on Non-interactive Deniable Secret Sharing from Indistinguishability Obfuscation
entry.summary: A Note on Non-interactive Deniable Secret Sharing from Indistinguishability Obfuscation IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies deniable secret sharing, in which shareholders who are forced to reveal their shares can each locally produce fake shares consistent with a fake secret of their choice, indistinguishable from real ones. The authors give a transformation that upgrades any secret sharing scheme for any access structure into a non-interactive deniable scheme, using a collusion-resistant constrained PRF that can be built from polynomially secure indistinguishability obfuscation and one-way functions. The share size overhead is polynomial in the number of shareholders, and using indistinguishability obfuscation directly with a somewhere-statistically binding hash reduces it to polylogarithmic.

entry.title: Faster homomorphic AES using mixed byte-bit data packing
entry.summary: Revisiting homomorphic AES evaluation with Hybrid Byte-Bit Packing IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies how to run AES inside BGV homomorphic encryption efficiently, a key benchmark for practical FHE. After computing the multiplicative inversion in SubBytes, the authors convert the packing from byte-oriented to bit-oriented and evaluate the affine and linear layers over GF(2) with homomorphic additions. The approach is implemented in HElib and reports per-block latency speedups of 2.1 to 11.7 times, depending on bootstrapping and hardware.

entry.title: Round-key equivalence and collisions in the revised MoFang cipher
entry.summary: Round-Key Equivalence and Collisions of the Revised MoFang IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026The paper proves that, in the revised MoFang reference implementation, certain restricted nonzero message patterns preserve per-round key cancellation, so each input has 16 round-key-equivalent inputs. It classifies the round key map, giving possible equivalence class sizes and necessary and sufficient conditions for the DM variants. It also gives an exact count of the covered domain for those variants.

entry.title: Homomorphic encryption and bootstrapping for real matrices in conjugate-invariant rings
entry.summary: Homomorphic Encryption and Bootstrapping for Real Matrices over Conjugate-Invariant Rings IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper builds a bootstrapping procedure for the conjugate-invariant CKKS scheme, factoring its transforms into sparse stages and needing no conjugation key. It also folds the three variables of the Gentry–Lee scheme under inversion to obtain matrix-product-closed subrings with real slots, and describes CI³-GL in detail. CI³-GL encrypts real matrices without conjugation and has keys of half the rank of GL keys for the same matrix size and count. The authors adapt GL's matrix-product bootstrapping to CI³-GL and report a prototype implementation.

entry.title: FALCON-PARE: Full-range side-channel key recovery of Falcon using prior-enhanced evidence
entry.summary: FALCON-PARE: Full-Range Side-Channel Key Recovery of Falcon via Prior-Enhanced Evidence IACR ePrint · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents FALCON-PARE, a framework that recovers the full secret key of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme by exploiting side-channel leakage from its NTT computations. It combines Falcon's discrete-Gaussian prior with leakage from range conversion and Montgomery multiplication, propagating the resulting soft evidence through the NTT factor graph. The authors evaluate the method on an STM32F407 microcontroller under two compiler settings, reporting single-trace full key recovery and substantially higher coefficient-wise accuracy than existing SASCA attacks.

entry.title: Classification of Quadratic APN Functions on F_2^10 with Prime-Order Self-Equivalence
entry.summary: Quadratic APN Functions of 𝔽₂¹⁰ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies quadratic APN functions on F_2^10 that have a self-equivalence of prime order, a class of functions with the lowest differential uniformity. The authors settle 298 of 299 types and find 29 classes up to extended affine equivalence, four of them new. The one open type consists of quadratic canonical triplicate functions.

entry.title: Inferring sensitive events in multi-mode cyber-physical systems through scheduling side channels
entry.summary: Inferring Sensitive Events in Multi-Mode Cyber-Physical Systems via Scheduling Side Channels arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper shows that cyber-physical systems that switch between operating modes create a timing side channel, because mode changes alter the interference experienced by co-running tasks. The authors present STAMP, a lightweight attack that requires no knowledge of task parameters or scheduling policy and lets an unprivileged co-resident observer infer modes from its own execution timing. It reports 94.7% accuracy on a ZoneMinder home-security deployment and 86.0% on ROS 2 AMCL with the Oxford RobotCar dataset. The paper also evaluates a schedule-randomization defense, reporting its effect on detection recall and on-time job completion.|

entry.title: Testing whether camera-noise fingerprints can be faked, with a detection toolkit
entry.summary: Evaluating the Robustness of PRNU Source-Camera Attribution to the Fingerprint-Copy Attack: An Open Toolkit with Triangle-Test Detection arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper examines whether PRNU, a sensor-noise fingerprint used to attribute images to source cameras, can be forged. The authors release prnucf, an open toolkit that implements the fingerprint-copy attack alongside a triangle-test detector and a cohort-calibrated decision procedure. In a controlled multi-camera Monte-Carlo benchmark, forgeries reached arbitrary target PCE at a mean PSNR of 59.2 dB, while the triangle test achieved an AUC of 0.999 and detected every forgery at a 5% false-positive operating point.

entry.title: Representational Geometry as a Diagnostic for Adversarial Robustness
entry.summary: Representational Geometry as a Diagnostic for Adversarial Robustness arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies multilayer perceptrons trained on MNIST under three adversarial training methods and compares them with a standard network. It uses M-PHATE to visualize how the geometry of the data changes during training, and measures displacement, maximum mean discrepancy, and nearest-neighbor recovery on penultimate-layer representations. The authors find that adversarial training changes how networks organize internal representations, and that robust accuracy and representational stability can rank the same defenses in opposite order.

entry.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks
entry.summary: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 13, 2026Weightless Neural Networks are lightweight classifiers that binarize inputs and store binary patterns in lookup memories, which makes them attractive for intrusion detection. The paper studies their adversarial robustness in WiSARD and in Bloom filter variants, showing that only perturbations crossing an encoding threshold can change predictions. Experiments on MNIST and on the Bot-IoT, CICIDS, and UNSW-NB15 intrusion datasets show that encoding granularity trades a small clean-accuracy loss for lower attack success, while adversarial perturbations still cause many attacks to be classified as normal traffic.

entry.title: Efficient Monte Carlo Privacy Accounting via Importance Sampling
entry.summary: Tractable Importance Sampling for Monte Carlo Privacy Accounting arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper addresses estimating tight differential privacy parameters for matrix factorization with privacy amplification by sampling, where the failure probability δ is hard to compute analytically. Standard Monte Carlo sampling has high variance for small δ, so the authors propose a shifted importance sampling proposal with a stretch factor α>1. They prove a closed-form bound B(α)<1 on the importance-weighted estimator's support and show the estimator fits the KL-Hoeffding verification protocol, reducing sample complexity by a factor of 1/B(α*).

entry.title: Fair, efficient EV charging coordination resistant to tampering, using threshold cryptography and machine learning
entry.summary: Fair and Efficient Distributed EV Charging Coordination Using Threshold Cryptography and Machine Learning arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies distributed electric vehicle charging coordination based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), which assumes all participants follow the algorithm. The authors show that malicious participants can send inconsistent signals or deviate from updates, and propose a framework combining threshold-signed broadcasts with upload recomputation to detect every deviation. Affected vehicles recover locally using a certified, fleet-aware machine learning price forecast. Simulations with real-world data show the defense keeps cost changes within 2.6% of benign operation.

entry.title: Online resource allocation that protects user privacy with differential privacy
entry.summary: Online Allocation with Differential Privacy arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies online allocation under limited resources where decisions must satisfy differential privacy to protect sensitive user information. It defines differential privacy notions suited to different requirements and establishes the fundamental performance limits of any algorithm under them. The authors propose PPOA, a privacy-preserving meta algorithm, give conditions under which it preserves joint or local differential privacy while achieving near-optimal performance, and present concrete designs analyzed in adversarial and stochastic settings. Numerical experiments on AI model routing in battery-powered edge systems demonstrate the proposed algorithms.

entry.title: I2C-GRPO: Checklist Rewards for Training LLM Agents on DDoS Alert Triage
entry.summary: I2C-GRPO: Insight Importance Checklist for Reinforcement Learning in a Multi-Agent DDoS Alert Triage Workflow arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of training LLM agents with reinforcement learning for cybersecurity alert triage, where intermediate steps lack verifiable labels. It proposes I2C-GRPO, which scores candidate investigative actions by how well they cover expert-ranked forensic insights. A Qwen3-4B agent trained on DARPA 2000 LLDOS 1.0 reportedly reaches a mean F1-score of 0.869 and a 4.9% false-positive rate on an independent CSE-CIC-IDS2018 DDoS trace. Claims are limited to DDoS alert triage.

entry.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? A Study of Weight-Space Programming Security
entry.summary: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper examines whether large language models can use weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks. Five general-purpose LLMs were asked to edit the weights of target models from natural-language instructions across an MLP, ResNet-18, and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. The experiments found that backdoors can be injected while largely preserving clean performance, sometimes with very few parameter changes, and that editing ability varies substantially across LLMs and architectures.

entry.title: Evolutionary transfer learning for physical attacks on autoencoder communication
entry.summary: Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning for Physical Attack on End-to-End Autoencoder Communications arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies physical attacks on end-to-end autoencoder communication systems, which can be fooled by manipulated transmitted signals. It proposes PAGA, a genetic-algorithm method for crafting attack signals in white-box settings, and PAMFGA, a multi-factorial variant for black-box settings where the receiver is largely unknown. The attacks are evaluated using reconstruction error and misclassification rates, and the experiments show they substantially reduce the reliability of the studied systems.

entry.title: Rethinking Adversarial Robustness Evaluation via Structural Gradient Alignment
entry.summary: Beyond Attack-Based Accuracy: Rethinking Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Through Structural Gradient Alignment arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes Structural Gradient Alignment (SGA), a metric for measuring visual adversarial robustness of models without relying on specific attacks. SGA uses a few randomly sampled, unlabeled public probes and needs only one input-gradient computation per model-probe pair. Tested across 38 DNNs, VLMs, and LVLMs, SGA produces model rankings consistent with attack-based references.

entry.title: Security analysis of anonymous authentication in Apple's Private Cloud Compute
entry.summary: Security Analysis of Anonymous Authentication in Apple's Private Cloud Compute IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines the custom authentication protocol behind Apple's Private Cloud Compute, which sends on-device tasks such as language-model prompts to the cloud. The authors formalize the goals such a protocol needs, including rate limiting, user anonymity, and accountability, under the name PORTA. They analyze Apple's protocol against these properties. They also propose an alternative based on anonymous credentials, which they state achieves all of them. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize PORTA, analyze Apple's protocol, and provide a provably secure anonymous-credential alternative.

entry.title: Security analysis of the cubic UOV variant CML
entry.summary: On the Security of the Cubic UOV Variant CML IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper analyzes CML, a cubic multivariate signature scheme over F_{2^8} designed to hide cubic term positions. The authors show that the cubic homogeneous parts of the public key span a space of dimension at most two, which leads to a procedure for recovering an equivalent key. Their implementation recovered an equivalent key in under 5 minutes for each tested parameter set, including the set targeting 256-bit security.

entry.title: Optimized Strategy and Two-Step Estimator for Solving LWE with Side-Channel Hints
entry.summary: Optimized Solving Strategy and Two-Step Estimator for LWE with Hints IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026Side-channel hints can lower the cost of solving the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem. The paper optimizes a two-step approach that applies BKZ reduction followed by final lattice sieving, jointly choosing block sizes, tour counts, and the sieving configuration. It also introduces a two-step estimator that predicts the reduced-basis profile and the probability of secret recovery. Experiments show the strategy significantly outperforms prior methods by Cao et al. and May and Nowakowski.

entry.title: Triads Below the ISA: Optimizing Cryptographic Software in CPU Microcode
entry.summary: Triads below the ISA: Optimizing Cryptographic Software in CPU Microcode IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper treats the programmable microcode layer of x86 processors as a distinct target architecture for cryptographic computation and tailors implementations to its state, operations, invocation interface, capacity, and scheduling resources. The authors apply this method on Intel Goldmont to Keccak-f[1600] and X25519. Their Keccak implementation cuts permutation latency by 7.36% versus the fastest native implementation compared. The complete X25519 implementation needs 7.3% fewer cycles than s2n-bignum and 9.8% fewer than OpenSSL.

entry.title: Encrypted authorship matching for fraud investigations
entry.summary: Encrypted Authorship Attribution for Fraud Detection IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026Authorship attribution links anonymous or disputed texts to known writers based on their writing style, which can help investigate phishing, impersonation, and investment scams. This paper studies privacy-preserving stylometric attribution using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), focusing on Burrows' Delta, a method based on token frequency statistics and z-score comparisons. The authors present a homomorphic implementation and show with the CKKS scheme that the full pipeline runs without bootstrapping while maintaining high numerical accuracy.
